front:
The input is a binary read-once branching program given by its list of vertices
and transitions. We want a deterministic estimate of its acceptance
probability. The construction reduces this task to evaluating sparse sampled
tables recursively. One proposed evaluator compares vertex names exactly and
uses \(O(\log n\log\log n)\) work bits for large input length \(n\). The
logarithmic-space proposal uses fingerprints for comparisons at tight space
budgets. Both space bounds remain conditional on the proof obligations below.

An \id{L-} routine defines an explicit finite computation. A \id{P-} routine
returns a digit, a port, a bounded action result, or another piece of the
low-space computation. The \id{T-} routines are physical programs that expose
the end of a path and own the information needed to return or discard it.
For a fixed task, seed, and comparison policy, prove that the physical
queries give the logical computation's values and finite decisions.
This lets the same logical accuracy argument serve both evaluators.
The interfaces state the required behavior and local state bounds.
The proof notes identify the checks needed to use them.

sections.title: Input, base graph, and exact target
Finite algebra used by the logical routines

blocks.tex:
The base graph and copied names set the domain for the exact hierarchy.
The remaining definitions specify the sampling law and the walk used in
the averages.

These definitions describe the finite data passed between the
logical algorithms. They also give the fields that physical replay
must recover.

sections.title: Physical state and finite arithmetic rules

blocks.tex:
These definitions specify how to account for a physical call and
which finite expression each query must compute.
These definitions apply to the ordinary logarithmic-space proposal.
\Needspace{12\baselineskip}

\Aref{L-AVERAGE} now returns ordered arrivals and their aggregate.
\Aref{L-CERT} evaluates the finite integer rules directly.
The loops in \Aref{L-PILOT} and \Aref{L-ESTIMATE} show their round and
group bodies. The two interface changes require correspondence
proofs for the physical enumerator and arithmetic stepper.

\paragraph{Notation.}
\(n\) is the input length. In Section~\ref{sec:walkthrough},
\(p,w,C,E\) are the continuation, reward, transition, and correction.
\(x,z,y\) are the source, midpoint, and destination.
\(f_l\) is the stage scale and \(\pi_{f_l}\) its hit probability.

operations.title: The logical product and the physical query

blocks.tex:
Start with the continuation equation \(p=w+Cp\). Here \(p\) is the
continuation probability vector, \(w\) is the accumulated reward, and \(C\)
is the remaining transition matrix. A correction matrix \(E\) changes
the reward to \(w+Ew\) and the transition matrix to \(C-E+EC\). The
continuation equation is preserved because
\[
  (w+Ew)+(C-E+EC)p=w+Cp+E(w+Cp-p)=p.
\]
The same product \(EC\) occurs while constructing the correction. A term
in its \((x,y)\) entry follows a correction edge from source \(x\) to
midpoint \(z\), then a transition from \(z\) to destination \(y\).

Sampling the midpoint saves work when the left factor has few enough
outgoing entries at the sampling scale. The right factor's weights must
also be small enough that increasing the weight of a sampled term keeps
the contribution controlled. This is the reason to reduce transition
weights before asking for a sparse recursive estimator. The vertex
sampling example in Vadhan's outline motivates these two requirements.

Take one valid product contribution at stage \(l\). For this example the
parent and transition bin both use the stage scale \(f_l\), so the
magnitude-bin weight in \Dref{D-WEIGHTS} is one. Suppose the sampled
correction and transition entries on this path are \(1/2\) and \(1/4\),
respectively. With the midpoint retained, their contribution to the
logical sample is \(f_l/(8\pi_{f_l})\), where \(\pi_{f_l}\) is the
midpoint hit probability. Averaging later includes the walk weight and
the sign of the child-budget difference. \Aref{L-FAMILY} and
\Dref{D-ROWFAMILIES} specify these operations separately.

\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*]
\item \Aref{P-CHILD} describes the two queries. The right query uses the
midpoint as its source and its task depends on the shared seed and the
right factor's parameters. All sources that use this right factor at
the same midpoint see the same table.
\item For a right-factor digit, \Aref{P-INTRINSICVALUE} calls
\Aref{P-CAP} at the source with the correction's outgoing port. On
success the cursor moves to \(z\) and the call returns the incoming
port that identifies the edge in reverse. The incoming cap makes that
port a bounded token.
\item \Aref{P-ROW} reads the requested digit of the transition entry at
\(z\) and restores the cursor to \(z\). \Aref{P-CAP} in inverse mode
then returns to \(x\). \Aref{P-NUMSTEP} combines the operand digits using
the product expression and its declared scale. A failed left move
contributes zero and leaves the cursor at \(x\).
\item \Aref{P-ARRIVAL} supplies the signed weighted digit for this
record. \Aref{P-MERGE} includes it with the other arrivals assigned to
its representative. Later queries use the resulting compressed row
and the fixed final ports.
\end{enumerate}

The logical product analysis uses the row cap on the transition table
to bound how many destinations reuse one left-factor error. It uses
the incoming cap on the correction table to bound how many sources
reuse one right-factor error at \(z\). The physical argument uses the
same capped relation to enumerate outgoing ports and restore the
cursor. These two arguments meet at the specification of one sampled
table. The exact transition matrix can have dense rows and columns.

The ingredient order explains the construction. Within a recursive call,
the order is different. A parent forms sample terms from completed
lower-budget tables, averages differences between child estimates,
then groups and compresses each increment. The final gates turn the
completed raw row into the next table. The degree bounds are therefore
both hypotheses on child tables and conclusions for the parent.

The correspondence proof uses a common induction on the call allowance.
Each local proof identifies its logical output, including ordered
representatives, padded ranks, and finite tests where relevant. Its physical
part accounts for live fields, restoring failure, and cleanup. The whole
proof can reuse the logical error estimates after these correspondences
are established. Section~\ref{sec:assembly} states how the pieces fit.

The full-space and exact-name configurations use the same input and
output convention. The workspace bound differs.

operations.title: Paired base graph and continuation values

blocks.tex:
The logical reference stores the base matrix \(S\) and reward \(e\).
The physical graph represents an edge by a port, a bounded index among
edges leaving or entering the current vertex. A forward or inverse
operation returns the opposite port. The extra chain vertices in the
base graph make both port sets bounded.

operations.proof:
Verify the probability-preserving base conversion, the
name convention, and both directions of the port pairing. Check the
setup ranges and halting behavior on malformed and zero-layer inputs.

operations.title: Sample vertices at a prescribed rate

blocks.tex:
Each filter is a membership predicate on a vertex name. The source,
destination, and midpoint roles use separate seeds. The next product
can use a previous task's source or destination filter as its midpoint
filter, with the role and rate changes in \Dref{D-CHILD}. The
finite field and hit law are specified in \Dref{D-SEEDS}.

operations.proof:
Establish the hit probabilities and the conditional pair
and count estimates for the actual nonzero-slope sampler.

operations.title: Walk on the conditioned seed set

blocks.tex:
\Dref{D-EXPANDER} specifies a walk that respects required hits and
frozen bits. \Dref{D-ACTION} and \Dref{D-SLOTS} give the concrete
candidate. A fixed word can be represented by affine maps and candidate
wraps before the endpoints are available. The valid wrap is identified
by a later test. This allows the word description to be held during
recursive evaluation.

operations.proof:
For use in the estimator, prove the exact word
lift, weight preservation, and identification of the conditional
law at each caller.

operations.title: Validate a sampled arrival

blocks.tex:
First establish that the candidate endpoint exists. Then test the
required hits and wraps at the original source and destination.
The \Aref{P-ENDPOINT} hit and wrap modes perform the local tests during
the visits from Section~\ref{sec:pointers}.

operations.proof:
Check that the tests implement the word and hit conditions
for both signs of a budget difference, with restoration on every
failed test.

blocks.tex:
A hard threshold illustrates the continuation-preserving update with
full arrays. The estimator's reference uses the smooth cutoff in
\Dref{D-CUTOFFS}.

operations.title: Detect crowded correction columns

blocks.tex:
The pilot asks which columns would acquire too many substantial
incoming entries during correction. It returns a fixed multiplier
for each column. These multipliers allow the next routine to restart
with a single frozen choice.

operations.proof:
Show that each enabled column has a bounded number of
substantial candidates at its scale, and that the columns requiring
copies can be counted from the total incidence bound.

operations.title: Compute the exact correction

blocks.tex:
At a fixed stage the correction uses the product of its preceding
iterate and the transition matrix. The cutoff leaves a positive
residual at corrected positions. This bounds the number of positions
that can contribute to a path in the iteration argument. The exact
correction is the reference for the common sampled estimator.

operations.proof:
Show that the fixed number of sweeps is sufficient,
that the residual is nonnegative and substochastic, and that fully
enabled columns meet the new entry bound.

operations.title: Divide the remaining large weights

blocks.tex:
When a column's correction is restricted, some residual entries can
still be large. Route those entries among copies, and apply the same
projection to the reward. The copy sample in
\Aref{L-FAMILY} and the copy branch of \Aref{T-INTRINSIC} implement
the corresponding queries.

operations.proof:
Check the projection identity, the new entry bound,
and the count of active copies.

operations.title: Compose the exact stages

blocks.tex:
The hierarchy uses the pilot, correction, and split at each stage.
Its primary-copy reward is the deterministic quantity that the sampled
reward vector estimates.

operations.proof:
Iterate the projection identity and bound the remaining
contribution at the primary copy using the shrinking entry bound and
the active-vertex count.

operations.title: Normalize the ideal sampled tables

blocks.tex:
At a magnitude scale the number of substantial entries in a row is
bounded by its mass divided by that scale. Sampling gives a bounded
expected degree. The gates enforce a bound on every seed and change the
mean. The ideal table divides by the conditional mean of the relevant
gates. This calculation supplies a comparison target for accuracy.

operations.proof:
Bound the normalizer away from zero where it is used and
check the conditional mean after dividing by it.

operations.title: Assemble final values and ports

blocks.tex:
For the computed table, first finish all raw rows of the task.
Their local scores define the incoming rank. A correction column
that fails the port count loses the entire column of ports.
These operations define the input relation for later products.
The implementation exposes a row by port and digit queries.

The class test uses a fixed prefix of the raw value and rank.
The incoming rank and its cutoff have separate roles. The rank
is recovered by the walks in Section~\ref{sec:reversible-walks}.
The correction's paired port is used whenever a destination query
has to return to its source.

operations.proof:
Show that the fixed classes cover the gated support, that
the cap deletes only zero gated values, and that each query agrees
with the corresponding finite test or value. Check that successful
pairs are inverse and that failure and cleanup restore all required
state.

operations.title: Form one sample term

blocks.tex:
For one lower budget, the family specification gives direct,
product, subtraction, copy, signal, detector, and reward
contributions. The child constructor fixes the task fields and
coefficients. A product uses two children under the same transformed
seed, as in Section~\ref{op:sampled-ec}.

The child constructor has a materialized view for the logical algorithm
and a relative view for the physical caller. The numerical query asks
only for the operand digit it needs. Its right-factor excursion keeps
the left edge's inverse token until the digit request returns.

operations.proof:
Check each family's term and coefficient against
\Dref{D-ROWFAMILIES} or \Dref{D-VECTORS}. Prove the conditional mean
and the error transfer from child values. The product bound uses
pointwise support counts and the common right tuple.

operations.title: Average differences and expose ordered arrivals

blocks.tex:
At each lower budget average the difference from the preceding estimate.
Earlier differences get longer walks. For a row, the grouped increment
has both an aggregate value and an ordered list of contributing records.
The list determines first representatives, multiplicities, and finite
expression order in the next ingredient.

operations.proof:
Identify the finite average with the valid word expansion and
bound its bias and centered error. Verify that the physical descriptors
give the same ordered records, including valid zero contributions.

operations.title: Accumulate detector and reward vectors

blocks.tex:
A vector task has one scalar per source. It adds each group of scalar
increments to the preceding prefix and clamps the result before
processing the next group. Detector rank is formed before averaging.
The final vector query is the scalar branch of \Aref{L-ESTIMATE}.

operations.proof:
Prove scalar-prefix correspondence and count the state held
across each old-prefix or arrival request.

operations.title: Group arrivals under the chosen policy

blocks.tex:
An old representative keeps its own old value. A class with no old
representative takes its first valid arrival as representative.
Every matching arrival contributes to the sum, even when that record
is not the representative. For example, if two distinct new endpoints
have equal fingerprints and there is no old representative, exchanging
their arrival order can change which endpoint receives the class sum.
This explains why the aggregate alone does not determine the row.

operations.proof:
Prove that the physical scan selects the same representatives
and adds the same signed operands in the fixed order, for the selected
policy.

operations.title: Choose a default and retain exceptions

blocks.tex:
Use the grouped row to compute the two thresholds and the new common
default. The compression formula clips each coordinate toward the
default. A fixed finite test decides which representatives to retain.
The ordered list, default, and coordinate expressions are used by the
next prefix or by final assembly.

operations.proof:
Bound the number of retained entries and the distortion
of the later row functions. Prove that the physical tests and streams
agree with the logical finite certificates, padded operand lists, and
ties. A later digit request must leave the chosen list fixed.

operations.title: Use an exact reference within a fingerprint block

blocks.tex:
For the full-space policy, analyze the change in grouping by an
explicit calculation with exact name comparison in the current block.
The computations below that block keep their specified comparison
policy. This is a reference calculation for the accuracy proof.

operations.proof:
Prove current-key independence of the reference candidates
and bound escaped candidates and propagated child errors. The fixed-pair
collision estimate is used only with the stated conditioning.

operations.title: Reconstruct a task from relative fields

blocks.tex:
A physical caller retains a short description of the child request
and uses shared scratch to reconstruct its parameters. The starting
point is the immutable root data. Each completed link specifies the
seed transformation and task update needed for the next link.

operations.proof:
Specify the concrete marked fields and prove replay on
both genuine and admitted probe views, with shared scratch erased
before a recursive query.

operations.title: Expose a port and own its return path

blocks.tex:
The logical operation maps a present port to an endpoint. Its physical
realization can leave the cursor at that endpoint and return a trace.
The trace owns any retained child path. Returning consumes the trace
and restores the source. Discarding consumes it at the endpoint.
This distinction lets the reversible walk see the terminal program's
own states.

operations.proof:
Give the finite transition and field catalogue for the
terminal programs. Check all presence, motion, return, discard, and
failure cases, including synthetic states admitted to a probe.

operations.title: Visit an endpoint and perform one action

blocks.tex:
A restoring visit exposes a port, performs a bounded action at its
endpoint, and returns. The endpoint action supplies the name bits and
hit or wrap tests used by the other ingredients. In full space it can
also access one shared fingerprint cell.

operations.proof:
Prove that the actions are repeatable at the selected
endpoint and that their paths and cleanup meet the restoration
contract.

operations.title: Compare names or fingerprints

blocks.tex:
The chosen policy gives a comparison predicate for \Aref{L-GROUP}.
Exact mode compares name bits. In the full-space mode at tight
allowance, a recomputed fingerprint indexes one bit in a shared array.
A flip at the first endpoint changes the bit read at the second
precisely when the fingerprints agree. The repeated flip and read
recover the answer and restore the array.

operations.proof:
Establish the predicate returned in each mode, restoration
for arbitrary initial shared bits, and the retained fields at each
visit. Analyze collision-induced changes on the logical side using
Section~\ref{op:block-reference}.

operations.title: Traverse a terminal computation graph

blocks.tex:
Regard an admitted terminal program state as a vertex of a finite
graph. A probe tests or crosses a local incidence. A contour of the
component of a success halt enumerates its marked initial states
and returns to the halt. This implements incoming access without
retaining the full source name.

operations.proof:
Show that the admitted incidence rules are consistent,
that the contour directions are inverse, and that it visits precisely
the required initials. Count the shared graph state and each probe's
additional live fields.

operations.title: Recover the padded incoming score rank

blocks.tex:
An explicit reference enumerates the completed score column,
quantizes the scores at the certificate place, and takes its padded
rank. The physical version counts matching initials by traversing
the score graph for each descending payload. The rank modes of
\Aref{P-INCOMING} expose its digits, and its gate mode applies the
cutoff after the rank has been defined.

operations.proof:
Match the quantized ranks and zero padding to the finite
reference. The graph owns the score payload and the scan must restore
the same destination and payload before it advances.

blocks.tex:
The logical computation fixes an integer certificate at each place.
The chosen finite rules determine the later tests, so the two
evaluators must agree on the certificate itself. The reference below
evaluates the equations in \Dref{D-NUMRECIPES} with explicit storage.

operations.title: Stream digits through bounded requests

blocks.tex:
The arithmetic stepper either returns a bounded result or names
the next operand digit it needs. The caller owns the resume state
and handles the operand request. The primitive code and the client
therefore have separate storage obligations.

operations.proof:
Prove agreement with the finite equations for every
primitive and client, including ties and scale shifts. Instantiate the
resume transitions, then count the fields across each operand call.
For a reciprocal, keep the originating place available while erasing
the long early word before a late operand request.

operations.title: Evaluate one trial for each admitted seed

blocks.tex:
The finishing law conditions only on the hit at the primary start.
Each admitted seed produces one grid numerator by streaming the
final reward and clipping the result. The full-space seed
enumeration retains the multiplicity of original fair-bit strings.

operations.proof:
Check that enumeration realizes the single conditioned
law in \Dref{D-ROOTLAW} and that each trial implements the fixed
stream and grid truncation.

operations.title: Select the lower median by scans

blocks.tex:
Each scan uses the same sequence of trials. Counting values at or
below each grid threshold suffices to return the lower median.

operations.proof:
Use the root moment bound under the enumerated law and
the hierarchy remainder to put a majority of grid values within
the target error. Check the space of one trial together with the
seed and median counters.

blocks.tex:
The logical estimator reads earlier tasks at smaller budgets. It
consumes the signed arrivals in groups, updates a represented row or
scalar prefix, and assembles the final outputs. Its ports and finite
tests are fixed before a physical caller asks for any digit.

operations.title: Run the estimator in either comparison mode

blocks.tex:
The root sets up the input, enumerates trials, and returns their
median. The row and vector interfaces implement the selected
\Aref{L-ESTIMATE} on every legal seed, under the correspondence and
restoration contracts.

operations.proof:
The shared work is to prove the accuracy induction for the
specified law, instantiate the terminal and arithmetic libraries,
and prove that they realize the finite reference. The exact-name
configuration additionally needs a complete retained-field assignment
at the relaxed metadata cost. The full-space configuration needs the
adaptive comparison estimates and a retained-field assignment at
unit metadata cost. The signed space condition in \Dref{D-RESOURCE}
counts the entire catalyst in shared storage and the other live
fields at each boundary. Both unconditional conclusions remain open.

blocks.tex:
These operations take complete finite arrays or lists. Their physical
clients use the query interfaces in the ingredient sections.

components.title: Exact continuation values
components.interface_title: Exact continuation values interface
components.interface:
An explicitly stored rational strictly forward matrix $S$ and terminal indicator $e$ determine one rational vector $p$. The result is the complete continuation vector, not an entry oracle. Repeated labelled edges have already been added to the corresponding matrix entry.

\textbf{State and cost.} Full vector and exact rational accumulator; no bit-space bound. Both finite loops decrease their remaining counts.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} $S\ge0$, $S\mathbf1\le\mathbf1$, terminal rewards only.\par

steps.tex: Set every coordinate of $p$ to zero.
For $x$ in reverse vertex order, set $v=e(x)$.
For each $y>x$, update $v\gets v+S_{xy}p(y)$; then set $p(x)=v$.
Return $p$.

components.title: Validate and choose finite root ranges
components.interface_title: Validate and choose finite root ranges interface
components.interface:
Return $\rho=(x,n,n_0,z_0,L,N,r,B,M,p,k_{\max},\eta,q,\text{constant tags})$ as immutable root data, or $(\bot,0)$. The input $x$ remains read-only, represented by access to its actual tape, not copied into $\rho$. All variable integer fields have $O(B)$ bits.

\textbf{State and cost.} A fixed number of $O(B)$ integers during pure work; scratch is erased before the root evaluator. No recursive estimator call.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Endmarked input; the numerical program constants are fixed, not advice.\par

steps.tex: Count the actual input length $n$ and scan every listed record. Reject malformed layers, labels, terminals or indices, using counters saturated at $n+1$ before arithmetic use.
\Invoke{P-BASE}{x,\mathrm{size},0}{n_0}; \Invoke{P-BASE}{x,\mathrm{start},0}{z_0}.
By bounded integer loops choose the least $L$ with $8^L\ge48n_0$, set $N=n_0d_0^L$, and choose the least $r\ge1$ with $2^{3r}\ge8N48^3$.

Set padded power-of-two $B=\Theta(\log(n+2))$, $M=c(B+L+r)$ and $k_{\max}$ as in \Dref{D-TASKS}. Compute the maximum legal name/rate bound. In exact mode choose $q$ by E-ADDRESSES with $X=C_X(B+L+M+r+2)$; the fixed layout constant $C_X$ encloses every root allowance and place. In full mode set $q=1$.
Scan $p\in[2^{c_pB},2^{c_pB+1}]$; test all divisors $2,\ldots,\lfloor\sqrt p\rfloor$ by integer division and select the first prime. If the interval is exhausted, return $(\bot,0)$.
Return $(\rho,1)$ only if this prime exceeds every checked bound.

components.title: Local access to the paired base graph
components.interface_title: Local access to the paired base graph interface
components.interface:
The current cursor is an original vertex or a merging-chain name $(y,i)$. Modes are size, start, reward, weight, presence, forward and inverse. The last two return a success bit and the actual opposite port, and move the cursor only on success. Pure modes do not move it. Parallel labels remain distinct.

\textbf{State and cost.} Pure $O(\log(n+2))$ scratch. A successful pair changes only the shared cursor and returns a bounded token; failure restores it. No recursive calls.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Well-formed input, or a bounded invalid-request branch.\par

steps.tex: Scan labelled input edges in input order; for each destination $y$ count its incoming edges $e_1,\ldots,e_k$.
The virtual vertices are the original vertices and $(y,i)$, $1\le i\le k$. The redirected edge $e_i$ ends at $(y,i)$ with weight $1/2$; chain edges $(y,i)\to(y,i+1)$ and $(y,k)\to y$ have weight one.
For size/start/reward/weight, rescan these finite records and return the requested scalar; invalid requests return zero.
For presence/forward/inverse, enumerate the at most two incidences in the requested direction at the cursor in label order and check $p$ before motion.
On a valid move, compute its opposite incidence ordinal by the same scans, update the cursor, and return $(1,p')$. Otherwise return $(0,0)$ at the original cursor.

components.title: Affine vertex membership
components.interface_title: Affine vertex membership interface
components.interface:
Return the exact channel-$c$ membership bit for the integer name $v$ and rate $a=16^{-k}$. Invalid channel, seed, name or rate returns zero. This routine is pure; it neither selects a new seed nor changes the current cursor.

\textbf{State and cost.} Fixed number of $O(B)$ words in shared pure scratch, cleared on all returns; no child call.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Legal names are smaller than $p$ and $p2^{-k}\ge1$.\par

steps.tex: Check the finite channel/rate ranges, canonical field coordinates and $a_1^c\ne0$.
Compute $L_a=\lceil p/2^k\rceil$.
For $i=1,\ldots,4$, compute $w_i=(a_{0,i}^c+va_{1,i}^c)\bmod p$ as its canonical residue.
Return $b=1$ iff all $0\le w_i<L_a$; erase scratch.

components.title: One step of the conditional finite action
components.interface_title: One step of the conditional finite action interface
components.interface:
The 512 generator slots and conditional-factor layout are fixed in \Dref{D-SLOTS}. Modes RAW and TEST use a fixed wrap $z$; RAW returns its full-space bijection without testing unknown endpoints, and TEST additionally returns its exact validity bit. Inverse mode uses the inverse affine map of that same fixed variant. Free auxiliary coordinates are selected by the public mask, never by their values.

\textbf{State and cost.} Pure $O(B)$ scratch; a returned seed lives only in the shared reconstruction buffer. No estimator query or saved per-frame seed.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} $H$ supplies public box sides and free-bit mask; TEST also supplies the endpoint names.\par

steps.tex: Decode $g$ as one of eight factors and one of 64 slots. Identity/absent factors leave the seed unchanged.
For a channel slot obtain its explicit integer elementary matrix $A$ and translation $c$ from \Dref{D-SLOTS}; set $a_1^+=Aa_1$ and $a_0^+=Aa_0+c+Lz\pmod p$.
In TEST mode compute $w=a_0+va_1\bmod p$ for the designated endpoint and set $b=\mathbf1\{w\in[0,L)^4,\ 0\le Aw+c+Lz<L\}$. In RAW mode set $b=\bot$.
For the auxiliary four-coordinate factor apply $w\gets Aw+c\bmod2^{\ell_{\rm aux}}$; for a residual factor flip its designated bit on flip slots. Leave every frozen bit fixed.
In inverse mode apply $A^{-1}$ and subtract the same $c+Lz$, or undo the auxiliary action. Return the new seed, inverse slot/variant data and $b$.

components.title: Endpoint-independent word variants
components.interface_title: Endpoint-independent word variants interface
components.interface:
$w$ is a complete word/variant description: each of its $h$ slots carries a 512-letter index and the bounded channel wrap. Return its resulting seed, conjunction of tests in TEST mode, and weight $\omega=512^{-h}$. RAW replay is endpoint independent. Reverse mode inverts the fixed variant, not an adaptively selected wrap.

\textbf{State and cost.} Word descriptor $O(h)$ bits belongs to the caller; reconstructed seed and field scratch are shared and erased before recursive evaluation. The reverse scan restores the seed.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} $h=O(d)$; complete word, legal factor mask and original owner conditions.\par

steps.tex: Set $\sigma^+=\sigma$, $b=1$ and $\omega=512^{-h}$; reject malformed or unused nonzero fields.
For each letter in forward order, \Invoke{P-SEEDSTEP}{\sigma^+,H,g_i,z_i,\mathrm{mode}}{\sigma',\bar g_i,b_i}; set $\sigma^+=\sigma'$ and conjoin the defined test bits.
In reverse mode instead scan letters in reverse order and call \Invoke{P-SEEDSTEP}{\sigma^+,H,g_i,z_i,\mathrm{inverse}}{\sigma\prime,\bar g_i,b_i}; replace $\sigma^+$ by $\sigma\prime$.
Return $(\sigma^+,b,\omega)$; failed tests retain zero contribution without changing the weight.

components.title: Validate original hits and all deferred wraps
components.interface_title: Validate original hits and all deferred wraps interface
components.interface:
Return the conjunction of syntax, intrinsic presence, original-owner source hit and all word-wrap tests. Destination tests use the descriptor's final endpoint; a signal uses the original narrow rate $\tau$, while first-coordinate families use broad rate $a$. Output precision is not an argument.

\textbf{State and cost.} $O(d)$ descriptor and test index, finite conjunction bit; visits own and erase their traces. No numerical accumulator or requested digit place is retained.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Original owner condition and fixed word/mask; all tests are finite and structural.\par

steps.tex: \Invoke{P-DESCRIPTOR}{\mathcal T,c}{D,b}; if $b=0$, return zero.
\Invoke{P-INTRINSICVALID}{\mathcal T,c}{b}; if $b=0$, return zero.
\Invoke{P-ENDPOINT}{\mathcal T,\mathrm{source\ hit}}{u}; for each applicable source/unrestricted wrap prefix call \Invoke{P-ENDPOINT}{\mathcal T,\mathrm{WRAP}(i)}{v_i}; conjoin these bits.
For a row, test the destination hit and each destination wrap by \Invoke{P-VISITINTRINSIC}{\mathcal T,c,\alpha_i}{u_i,v_i}, where $\alpha_i$ contains the original owner's rate and prefix.
For a vector omit destination visits. Return the conjunction after every started visit has returned.

components.title: Dense hard-threshold example
components.interface_title: Dense hard-threshold example interface
components.interface:
Return one dense hard-threshold correction stage. The parameter $K$ is supplied, not chosen from an asymptotic slogan. The procedure makes no detector or sampling calls; its role is to explain the value-preserving correction identity.

\textbf{State and cost.} Three full matrices, vectors and loop counters; finite $K$ iterations. No physical estimator uses this routine.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Forward substochastic $0\le C\le f$ and $p=w+Cp\in[0,1]^V$ with $w\ge0$.\par

steps.tex: Set $E=0$.
For $i=1,\ldots,K$: \Invoke{L-MATMUL}{E,C}{Z}; for all $(x,y)$ set $E_{xy}\gets\max(0,C_{xy}+Z_{xy}-\theta f)$.
\Invoke{L-MATMUL}{E,C}{Z}; set $D=C-E+Z$ entry by entry.
\Invoke{L-MATMUL}{E,w}{v}; set $w^+=w+v$ and return $(D,w^+)$.

components.title: Sampled detector and frozen multiplier
components.interface_title: Sampled detector and frozen multiplier interface
components.interface:
$\Omega$ explicitly lists the independent channel seeds, their hit bits at every vertex, and their uniform multiplicities. This call returns all exact detector values and the final column multiplier. Every expectation below is computed by summing over the indicated nonempty sublist, including duplicate encodings.

\textbf{State and cost.} All pilot matrices, seed tables and detector arrays may be stored. Finite rounds, seeds, vertices and ranks ensure termination.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Finite sampler table with positive one-hit probabilities; legal rank constants.\par

steps.tex: Set $\widehat E=0$ and $u_{0,y}=0$.

In each round $i=1,\ldots,K$ do the following.
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=1.7em,itemsep=2pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item \Invoke{L-MATMUL}{\widehat E,C}{Z}. Set $G=C+Z$.
\item For every seed $\sigma$ and row $x$, form $v=(G_{xz}/f:Y_f(z)=1)$; \Invoke{L-RANK}{v,k_{\rm row},0}{s}; set $r_x(\sigma)=\rho(s)$.
\item For every $(\sigma,y)$ form $v=(\phi(G_{xy}/f)r_x(\sigma):X_f(x)=1)$; \Invoke{L-RANK}{v,j_{\rm det},0}{b_{\sigma,y}}.
\item For each $y$, sum $b_{\sigma,y}$ over $Y_f(y)=1$ and divide by that sublist's length to obtain $u_{i,y}$.
\item Scan $h=1,\ldots,i$ for the largest $u_{h,y}$; set $\widehat g_{i,y}=\gamma(\max_hu_{h,y})$ and $\widehat E_{xy}=fQ(G_{xy}/f)\widehat g_{i,y}$.
\end{enumerate}
Return $(\widehat g_K,u)$ and discard $\widehat E$.

components.title: Correction with a frozen column multiplier
components.interface_title: Correction with a frozen column multiplier interface
components.interface:
$g\in[0,1]^V$ is frozen throughout this call. The smooth scalar function $Q$ is the fixed polynomial cutoff in \Dref{D-CUTOFFS}. Return the final correction, its residual, and the updated reward. No requirement $E\le C$ is imposed.

\textbf{State and cost.} Explicit arrays and one finite iteration counter. No seed or numerical precision is an input.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} The same matrix/reward hypotheses as L-DENSE; fixed legal thresholds and $K$.\par

steps.tex: Set $E=0$.
For $i=1,\ldots,K$: \Invoke{L-MATMUL}{E,C}{Z}; set $G=C+Z$ and $E_{xy}=fQ(G_{xy}/f)g_y$ entry by entry.
\Invoke{L-MATMUL}{E,C}{Z}; set $D=C-E+Z$.
\Invoke{L-MATMUL}{E,w}{v}; set $w^+=w+v$; return $(E,D,w^+)$.

components.title: Weighted node splitting
components.interface_title: Weighted node splitting interface
components.interface:
The input $u$ is the complete detector array from the pilot. A copied name is $x\alpha$ with $0\le\alpha<d_0$. Return complete copied arrays and the projection matrix $P$; primary copies preserve the old target because their multiplier is one.

\textbf{State and cost.} Complete copied arrays, with $d_0$ fixed. Scalar cutoffs use exact rational arithmetic.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} $D,w^+$ are an L-CORRECT result with the matching pilot array and scale.\par

steps.tex: For each $x$, scan the detector rounds and let $v_x=\max_hu_{h,x}$; set $r_0(x)=1$ and $r_\alpha(x)=\chi_{1/4,1/2}(v_x)$ for $\alpha>0$.
For each $x\alpha,y\beta$, put $h=\chi_{1/128,1/64}(D_{xy}/f)$ and $s_\beta=1-(1-d_0^{-1})h$ if $\beta=0$, otherwise $h/d_0$.
Set $C^+_{x\alpha,y\beta}=r_\alpha(x)D_{xy}s_\beta$, $w^{++}_{x\alpha}=r_\alpha(x)w^+_x$, and $P_{x\alpha,x}=r_\alpha(x)$; all other entries of $P$ are zero.

components.title: The exact reward hierarchy
components.interface_title: The exact reward hierarchy interface
components.interface:
The seed law and all constants are fixed once for the whole hierarchy. Each new $\Omega_l$ is the same law evaluated on the new legal names, not a fresh randomness choice. Return the entire final reward and the all-primary descendant of the input start. The explicit input $\Omega$ covers the finite name universe at every level; $\Omega_l$ is only its stored subtable for level $l$.

\textbf{State and cost.} Logical arrays grow with the copy universe; exactly $L$ stages. The algorithm is finite, not a low-space evaluator.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Paired base data and the simultaneous stage constants.\par

steps.tex: Set $(C_0,w_0)=(S,e)$ and let $z_0$ be the given start.
For $l=0,\ldots,L-1$, put $f=16^{-l}$.
\Invoke{L-PILOT}{C_l,f,\Omega_l,K}{g,u}.
\Invoke{L-CORRECT}{C_l,w_l,f,g,K}{E,D,w^+}.
\Invoke{L-SPLIT}{D,w^+,f,u}{C_{l+1},w_{l+1},P_l}; set $z_{l+1}=z_l0$.
Return $(w_L,z_L)$.

components.title: An ideal normalized sampled row
components.interface_title: An ideal normalized sampled row interface
components.interface:
The inputs are the deterministic normalized entries $d_{xy}$, a column multiplier, rates and an explicit seed/hit table. Return the full ideal normalized table at every seed. The conditional denominator includes precisely its numerator gates. This is an unbiasedness comparison object, not the implemented estimator.

\textbf{State and cost.} Full arrays over seeds and vertices, unrestricted rational storage; finite loops.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} $a\sum_y d_{xy}\le m_0$; for corrections, $g_y>0$ implies at most $r_0/u$ entries above $\theta/8$ in column $y$.\par

steps.tex: For every seed and row, form $v=(d_{xz}:Y_a(z)=1)$; \Invoke{L-RANK}{v,k_{\rm row},0}{s_x}; set $I_{xy}=I_\theta(d_{xy},s_x)$.
For each correction column form $v=(I_{xy}:X_u(x)=1)$; \Invoke{L-RANK}{v,k_c,0}{r_y}; set $T_y=1-\chi_{1/4,1/2}(r_y)$. For bins set $T_y=1$.
For each $(x,y)$ sum $h_\theta(d_{xy})R_\theta(s_x)T_y$ over $X_u(x)Y_\tau(y)=1$ and divide by the number of these seed encodings; call the result $q_{xy}$.
For every seed return $F_{xy}=X_u(x)Y_\tau(y)k(d_{xy})R_\theta(s_x)T_yg_y/\operatorname{clip}_{[1/2,1]}q_{xy}$.

components.title: Assemble final tables from completed row before gatings
components.interface_title: Assemble final tables from completed row before gatings interface
components.interface:
$C,z,O$ are completed raw arrays, defaults and lists for all rows of one task. Return final values and the fixed outgoing relation. This call performs no further raw-row construction. It may compute the strictly lower-budget detector vectors needed by a correction main.

\textbf{State and cost.} Complete raw arrays, incoming lists and detector arrays; finite ranks and lower-budget calls.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Completed row before gatings; preparation, main, score and vector owner cases are distinct.\par

steps.tex: For a vector return its clipped scalar and no ports immediately; the remaining steps are row cases.
For each row, \Invoke{L-RANK}{(C^1_{xy}:y\text{ on the broad hit}),k_{\rm row},z_x}{s_x}.

For each class test, \Invoke{L-CERT}{E_{C^1/H_1},P_*}{N_v}; \Invoke{L-CERT}{E_{s/H_1},P_*}{N_s}; put $\widetilde v=H_1N_v2^{-P_*}$ and $\widetilde s=H_1N_s2^{-P_*}$. Form $A$ using $\widetilde v>3\theta/8$, $\widetilde s<\theta/200$, and $A_I$ using $\widetilde v>\theta/10$, $\widetilde s<\theta/40$, together with the broad hit.

For each correction column, form its $I_\theta(C^1_{xy},s_x)$ list; \Invoke{L-RANK}{v,k_c,0}{r_y}; set $T_y=1-\chi_{1/4,1/2}(r_y)$. Count $A$ entries and delete the whole column when the count exceeds $k_c$.
For each required detector round $h$, \Invoke{L-ESTIMATE}{\mathcal T[U_{l,h};\mathsf T,f_l,t;m-c_{\rm col}],\eta}{U_h}; set $g_y=\gamma(\max_hU_h(y))$ by a finite scan.
Set score $=\phi(v)R(s)$; preparation $=h(v)R(s)T$; main $=X_\tau k_O(v)R(s)Tg/\operatorname{clip}_{[1/2,1]}(C^2/\zeta)$, on its final relation. Omitted bin factors equal one.
Return all final values, canonical expressions and fixed relations.

components.title: Rank the completed row before gating
components.interface_title: Rank the completed row before gating interface
components.interface:
Return a digit of the completed raw first-coordinate rank at final slack 1, using $k$ additional default operands. The raw port alphabet has fixed size $2^{c_2}$. Final gates, column caps and detector multipliers are not consulted.

\textbf{State and cost.} Constant-size port/rank indices and numerical state; all operands at final slack. No stored list.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} $k$ is one of the fixed local ranks; completed raw representation.\par

steps.tex: Start the finite padded-rank expression in an empty numerical state. Set $s=\varnothing,a=\bot$.
Repeat \Invoke{P-NUMSTEP}{E_{\rm rawrank},t,\mathrm{digit},s,a}{s',o}; set $s=s'$.
For each port operand, \Invoke{P-RAWNUM}{\mathcal T[1],p,\mathrm{presence},0}{v}; on success \Invoke{P-RAWNUM}{\mathcal T[1],p,\mathrm{coordinate}(1),j}{a}.
For absent/padding operands, \Invoke{P-RAWNUM}{\mathcal T[1],0,\mathrm{default}(1),j}{a}.
On DONE$(b)$ erase state and return $b$.

components.title: Fixed structural row classes
components.interface_title: Fixed structural row classes interface
components.interface:
Return the fixed structural membership bit for class $A$ or $A_I$. Choose the constant place $P_*$ once with $6H_1 2^{-P_*}\le\delta_0/10000$. Approximate raw value and rank by their complete signed prefixes at that place, rescaled by $H_1$. Equality at a threshold rejects.

\textbf{State and cost.} Fixed prefix words, one raw port and finite flags. Destination visit restores before return; no caller numerical precision is stored.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Legal class kind and owner threshold; all-seed raw range.\par

steps.tex: \Invoke{P-RAWNUM}{\mathcal T[1],p,\mathrm{presence},0}{v}; if absent or source-failed, return zero.
For $j=0,\ldots,P_*$, \Invoke{P-RAWNUM}{\mathcal T[1],p,\mathrm{coordinate}(1),j}{a_j}; \Invoke{P-RAWRANK}{\mathcal T,k_{\rm row},j}{b_j}; accumulate the two fixed-length rational prefixes.
For $A$ test $\widetilde v>3\theta/8$ and $\widetilde s<\theta/200$; for $A_I$ test $\widetilde v>\theta/10$ and $\widetilde s<\theta/40$.
\Invoke{P-VISITRAW}{\mathcal T[1],p,\mathrm{HIT}(\mathsf T,a,t)}{u,h}; return the conjunction of the two strict tests, $u$ and $h$.

components.title: Pre-incoming row functions
components.interface_title: Pre-incoming row functions interface
components.interface:
Return a digit of the specified local pre-incoming quantity: witness $I$, preparation, pilot score, or main prevalue. The first three have scale one; main prevalue has scale $H_*$. The denominator uses this owner's completed second coordinate before gating, not a fresh preparation call.

\textbf{State and cost.} Port, kind, fixed expression path and bounded pending digits; each endpoint mask is a restoring visit. No completed coordinate before gating is retained.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Correct owner/kind combination; fixed ranges and scale at every expression node.\par

steps.tex: \Invoke{P-CLASS}{\mathcal T,p,A_I\text{ for }I\text{, else }A}{v}; if $v=0$, return zero.
Set $s=\varnothing,a=\bot$ for the local expression. Repeat \Invoke{P-NUMSTEP}{E_{\rm local},t,\mathrm{digit},s,a}{s\prime,o}; set $s=s\prime$.
For coordinate before gating leaves call \Invoke{P-RAWNUM}{\mathcal T[1],p,\mathrm{coordinate}(\nu),j}{a}, using the explicit scale adapter in $E$.
For rank leaves call \Invoke{P-RAWRANK}{\mathcal T,k_{\rm row},j}{a}.
For the narrow mask call \Invoke{P-VISITRAW}{\mathcal T[1],p,\mathrm{HIT}(\mathsf T,\tau,t_{\rm suffix})}{u,a}; a failed visit supplies zero.
On DONE$(b)$ erase the numerical state and return $b$.

components.title: Delete an entire overfull incoming column
components.interface_title: Delete an entire overfull incoming column interface
components.interface:
Forward maps a present source port to its destination and actual incoming rank; inverse maps that destination/rank back to the source and port. Delete an entire column when its number of precursor initials exceeds $k_c$. Count present zero-valued ports. Failure restores the starting cursor.

\textbf{State and cost.} One graph region, bounded counts/rank/direction and one finite status. The cap does not own a second graph or score payload; all failed scans are undone.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Common precursor graph; $k_c$ fixed and PROBE/TOUR total.\par

steps.tex: For FORWARD, \Invoke{P-CLASS}{\mathcal T,p,A}{v}; if false fail. Initialize the canonical precursor initial $I(x,p)$ in one graph region.

From this initial repeat \Invoke{P-TOUR}{G,\mathrm{backward}}{z} until sentinel or $k_c+1$ jumps; count $a$. Undo exactly those jumps by \Invoke{P-TOUR}{G,\mathrm{forward}}{z}. Then count forward distance $b$ using \Invoke{P-TOUR}{G,\mathrm{forward}}{z} and undo with \Invoke{P-TOUR}{G,\mathrm{backward}}{z}.

If either scan overflowed or $a+b-1>k_c$, erase the restored initial and fail. Otherwise repeat \Invoke{P-TOUR}{G,\mathrm{forward}}{z} exactly $b$ times to the sentinel; return success with token $a$.

For INVERSE initialize the success sentinel at the destination. Repeat \Invoke{P-TOUR}{G,\mathrm{forward}}{z}, counting initials until sentinel or $k_c+1$ initials. On overflow undo exactly the recorded jumps with \Invoke{P-TOUR}{G,\mathrm{backward}}{z}.

At the restored sentinel reject overflow or an out-of-range token. Otherwise repeat \Invoke{P-TOUR}{G,\mathrm{forward}}{z} exactly $p$ times; read the actual source port at the resulting initial, erase graph work and return it.

components.title: Incoming score rank without a saved endpoint
components.interface_title: Incoming score rank without a saved endpoint interface
components.interface:
Kinds are DETECTOR-RANK, I-RANK and GATE. Rank kinds return the corresponding incoming rank digit. GATE returns a digit of $1-\chi_{1/4,1/2}(r)$ for the incoming-$I$ rank $r$. The rank scan and local gate arithmetic now have separate interfaces.

\textbf{State and cost.} Rank mode adds only finite control; gate mode adds a fixed numerical continuation. All destination tours restore before another rank digit is requested.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Correct uncapped score graph and all-seed rank/cutoff ranges.\par

steps.tex: For a rank kind, \Invoke{P-INCOMINGRANK}{\mathcal T,\mathrm{kind},t}{b}; return $b$.
For GATE start the fixed complementary-cutoff expression with $s=\varnothing,a=\bot$ and repeat \Invoke{P-NUMSTEP}{E_{\rm gate},t,\mathrm{digit},s,a}{s',o}; set $s=s'$.
For its rank REQUEST$(j)$, \Invoke{P-INCOMINGRANK}{\mathcal T,\mathrm{I\!\!\!-RANK},j}{a}.
On DONE$(b)$ erase state and return $b$.

components.title: Final numerical row query
components.interface_title: Final numerical row query interface
components.interface:
Return one digit of the final row value at public scale $H_*$. Dense bins/scores have only their local factor. Correction preparations multiply by their incoming gate, and correction mains additionally multiply by the detector cutoff. Missing capped ports return zero.

\textbf{State and cost.} Port, numerical continuation and one actual bounded inverse token; no source identifier or complete left value. The detector child decreases budget by $c_{\rm col}$.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Complete row task; both directions of the common cap are total.\par

steps.tex: For a dense owner choose the local-only expression with its scale adapter and skip the cap test; for a correction choose its local/gate/multiplier product.
For a correction only, \Invoke{P-CAP}{\mathcal T,p,\mathrm{forward}}{v,r}; on failure return zero; otherwise \Invoke{P-CAP}{\mathcal T,r,\mathrm{inverse}}{v',p'}.
Set $s=\varnothing,a=\bot$. Drive \Invoke{P-NUMSTEP}{E_{\rm row},t,\mathrm{digit},s,a}{s\prime,o}, replacing $s$ by $s\prime$.
For a local leaf call \Invoke{P-LOCAL}{\mathcal T,p,\mathrm{owner\ kind},j}{a}.

For a gate or detector leaf, freshly call \Invoke{P-CAP}{\mathcal T,p,\mathrm{forward}}{v,r}. On success call \Invoke{P-INCOMING}{\mathcal T,\mathrm{gate},j}{a}, or \Invoke{P-VECTOR}{\mathcal T[U_{l,h};\mathsf T,f_l,t_{\rm suffix};m-c_{\rm col}],j}{a}, as selected by the literal expression; then \Invoke{P-CAP}{\mathcal T,r,\mathrm{inverse}}{v',p'}.
A failed visit supplies zero. On DONE$(b)$ return only after all visits have restored.

components.title: The finite sample expressions
components.interface_title: The finite sample expressions interface
components.interface:
$\tau$ selects Base, direct, product, subtraction, copy, signal, detector, direct reward or product reward. Return the complete sample array and its ordered contributing records at child budget $r$. The seed is already the common transformed seed for this sample. The family is zero when $r\le0$, except the separately inserted Base term.

\textbf{State and cost.} All child arrays, expressions and provenance records are materialized. Recursion decreases the statistical budget; matrix and rank helpers are finite.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Legal owner/family pair; the parent chooses $r<m$ and the correct scale cost.\par

steps.tex: If $r\le0$ and $\tau\ne\mathrm{Base}$, return zero with no records.
\Invoke{P-CHILD}{\mathcal T,\tau,r,\mathrm{all}}{Q}; $Q$ contains the child tuples and scalar coefficients, or INVALID.
For each tuple $q$ in the returned fixed list, \Invoke{L-ESTIMATE}{q,\eta}{R_q}; retain its full array and expressions.
For direct/subtraction/signal, multiply the indicated child array by its returned coefficient, entry by entry. For copy, multiply the routed array by the returned copy-detector cutoff at each source.
For a row product or reward product, \Invoke{L-MATMUL}{A,B}{Z}, where $A$ is the left child with its midpoint mask and $B$ the common right child; multiply by the returned coefficient.
For detector, at each destination form the incoming score list and \Invoke{L-RANK}{v,j_{\rm det},0}{F_y}. For direct reward use the returned lower reward and copy factor.
Return these arrays with separate records for every contributing midpoint/port and the corresponding finite expression trees; Base uses the explicit $S$ or $e$ in $\mathcal T$.

components.title: Construct a child task with explicit field resets
components.interface_title: Construct a child task with explicit field resets interface
components.interface:
This pure constructor returns child task fields and exact scalar coefficients, never an estimator value. The complete output cases are in \Dref{D-CHILD}. A physical caller requests one field or one relative schema at a time; a logical caller may request the full fixed list. Invalid owner/tag/side or negative-stage requests return INVALID before any cursor change.

\textbf{State and cost.} $O(B)$ pure reconstruction scratch, erased before any estimator query. Returned physical schema is a relative view into a completed descriptor; its exact marked encoding remains U-CATALOG.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Complete task/descriptor, selected family, legal rates; no estimator access.\par

steps.tex: Check the owner, family, scale offset, copy symbols and child budget against \Dref{D-DESCRIPTOR} and \Dref{D-TASKS}.
For direct, subtraction or signal, copy the specified parent fields and overwrite owner, round, broad/usage rate and budget with the explicit \Dref{D-CHILD} row.

For product, construct LEFT and RIGHT separately: set roles to $(\mathsf S,\mathsf M,\mathsf T)$ and $(\mathsf M,\mathsf T,\mathsf S)$; RIGHT gets source rate $f_l$, source suffix empty, usage $\min(a,b)$, and no old-source or port field.

For copy or reward, require $l>0$, decrement $l$, prepend the known source/destination copy symbols to their suffixes, and set the residual route to the destination symbol. Detector children get intrinsic rate $f_{l-1}$.
For detector, construct the score tuple with roles $(c+1,c,c+2)$, rates all $f_l$, source suffix empty and destination suffix $s$.
Compute $w_b=(b/a)\pi_a/\pi_{\min(a,b)}$ and the other listed rational coefficients from public integers. Return the requested part of $Q$ and clear scratch.

components.title: Answer one digit of a sample expression
components.interface_title: Answer one digit of a sample expression interface
components.interface:
Return one normalized digit of the complete descriptor contribution, with the coefficient and leaf expression specified in \Dref{D-INTRINSIC}. Wrong coordinates return the zero stream without changing presence. This interface assumes the caller has validated the outer descriptor; its own lower leaf accesses still validate their public ports.

\textbf{State and cost.} Descriptor, fixed arithmetic continuation, one pending digit and at most one actual token. Coefficient/replay scratch is erased before child calls; signed arithmetic and structural charges compose in E-INTRINSICVALUE.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Valid descriptor, coordinate, normalized ranges; scalar families have no endpoint mode.\par

steps.tex: Start $s=\varnothing,a=\bot$ for expression $E_{\mathcal T,c,\nu}$ at scale $H_d$.
Repeat \Invoke{P-NUMSTEP}{E_{\mathcal T,c,\nu},t,\mathrm{digit},s,a}{s',o}; set $s=s'$.
For REQUEST$(\mathrm{row},j)$ call \Invoke{P-ROW}{\mathcal T_{\rm leaf},p,j}{a}; for REQUEST$(\mathrm{vector},j)$ call \Invoke{P-VECTOR}{\mathcal T_{\rm leaf},j}{a}.
For REQUEST$(\mathrm{rank},j)$ call \Invoke{P-INCOMING}{\mathcal T_{\rm score},\mathrm{detector},j}{a}.

For a right-factor request first \Invoke{P-CAP}{\mathcal T_L,p_1,\mathrm{forward}}{u,r}. If $u=0$, supply zero. Otherwise call \Invoke{P-ROW}{\mathcal T_R,p_2,j}{a} for a right row or \Invoke{P-VECTOR}{\mathcal T_R,j}{a} for a right vector, then \Invoke{P-CAP}{\mathcal T_L,r,\mathrm{inverse}}{v,p\prime} before resuming.
For copy leaves remove/restore the known source symbol around each call. On DONE$(b)$ erase $s$ and return $b$.

components.title: Average successive improvements
components.interface_title: Average successive improvements interface
components.interface:
$F_r(\sigma)$ is the materialized family at budget $r$, including its
contributing records and canonical expressions, with $F_0=0$.
$H$ gives the endpoint conditions for each output slice and the public
fixed-bit mask. $G$ specifies the \Dref{D-SLOTS} action. Return the aggregate
increment $\Delta$ in each dyadic group, zero outside $H$. For a row
task also return $J$, the ordered, signed arrival records for each
group, seed, and source. Each record includes its complete
\Dref{D-DESCRIPTOR} code, endpoint, and weighted expression. The full code
order fixes the order within a row. Retain valid zero contributions
and distinct codes with the same endpoint or effective seed.
For vectors the aggregate is scalar at each source and the record-list
output is empty.

\textbf{State and cost.} Complete finite arrays and explicit word and
record lists. The caller provides all queried lower-budget values.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Fixed legal $H,G$ and integer cost $c\ge1$; the finite seed encoding domain is explicit.\par

steps.tex:
For each output slice, initialize its kernel $K$, aggregate
  arrays, and record lists to zero or empty, then do the following.
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=1.7em,itemsep=2pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item For every admitted seed $\sigma$ and one-letter variant $w$,
    call \Invoke{P-WORD}{\sigma,H,w,\mathrm{TEST}}{\sigma',b,\omega}.
    Add $\omega$ to $K_{\sigma,\sigma'}$ when $b=1$.
  \item For $r=1,\ldots,M-c$, set $h=M-r$ and choose the group $d$
    with $d\le h<2d$. Form the column $v=F_r-F_{r-1}$.
    Apply \Invoke{L-MATMUL}{K,v}{v'} for $\ell_{\rm mix}h$ steps,
    replacing $v$ by $v'$ each time. Add $v$ to group $d$.
  \item For a row, expand each of those walk sums. At budget $r$
    and seed $\sigma$, enumerate every length-$\ell_{\rm mix}(M-r)$
    variant $w$ and call
    \Invoke{P-WORD}{\sigma,H,w,\mathrm{TEST}}{\sigma',b,\omega}.
    For a passing variant, use the present records in $F_r(\sigma')$
    with weight $\omega$ and in $F_{r-1}(\sigma')$ with weight
    $-\omega$. Attach the corresponding code, sign, and weighted
    expression to each record in group $d$.
  \end{enumerate}

Return $\Delta$ and $J$ with row records ordered by complete
  code and with zero aggregates and empty lists outside the slice.

components.title: Generate a complete candidate description
components.interface_title: Generate a complete candidate description interface
components.interface:
Decode one fixed-width candidate code, not an iterator with a hidden consumer. Return its typed fields $D$ and validity bit $b$. This checks syntax and owner/family compatibility only; it does not test endpoint presence, hits, wraps or numerical value.

\textbf{State and cost.} One $C_{\rm desc}d$-bit code and finite decode flags; public reconstruction scratch is erased. No graph query.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Dyadic slack in the task range; complete code.\par

steps.tex: \Invoke{P-REPLAY}{\mathcal T,\mathrm{descriptor\ bounds},0}{Q}.
Check that $c$ has exactly $C_{\rm desc}d$ bits and decode fields in \Dref{D-DESCRIPTOR} order; reject negative zero and nonzero unused fields.
For Base require $l=0$, $d=D$, a labelled base port and all word/budget fields zero.
Otherwise require $d\le h<2d$, $h\le m-1$, $\mu=m-h-\epsilon\ge0$, and the displayed family cost at most $h$.
Check the owner/tag table, copy symbols, ports, scale exponent, used word length and each letter/wrap range.
Return $(D,1)$ if all tests pass, otherwise $(\bot,0)$.

components.title: One validated increment value
components.interface_title: One validated increment value interface
components.interface:
Return a signed digit of one complete signed arrival. Its candidate identity is retained even if another candidate has the same endpoint or effective seed. The canonical zero stream is returned for invalid descriptors and wrong coordinates.

\textbf{State and cost.} One descriptor and finite validity flag coexist with the numerical child; no second value or endpoint is retained.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Complete owner handle; no cached validity promise is accepted.\par

steps.tex: \Invoke{P-VALID}{\mathcal T,c}{v}; if $v=0$, return zero.
\Invoke{P-INTRINSICVALUE}{\mathcal T,c,\nu,t}{b}.
Return $b$ after the intrinsic query restores.

components.title: Scalar prefixes for vector tasks
components.interface_title: Scalar prefixes for vector tasks interface
components.interface:
Return a digit of the vector's clipped scalar prefix at slack $d$, normalized by $H_d$. The vector uses every scalar arrival and no endpoint grouping. At the top the old prefix is zero; active $W_0$ is the exact base reward.

\textbf{State and cost.} $O(d)$ descriptor/list frontier plus numerical state; no endpoint list, representative code or retained matrix value.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Vector task and dyadic slack; full-sum normalization valid on all seeds.\par

steps.tex: For inactive/source-failed tasks return zero. For $W_0$ use the public reward expression; otherwise use the sum-and-clamp expression $E_{\rm scalar}$.
Start $s=\varnothing,a=\bot$ and repeat \Invoke{P-NUMSTEP}{E,t,\mathrm{digit},s,a}{s',o}; set $s=s'$.
For an OLD request, supply zero at the top; otherwise \Invoke{P-SCALARPREFIX}{\mathcal T,2d,j+\lambda d}{a} through the old-scale adapter.
For a descriptor request $(c,j)$, \Invoke{P-ARRIVAL}{\mathcal T,c,1,j}{a}, including every sign and zero-valued valid term.
On DONE$(b)$ erase the state and return $b$.

components.title: Final reward or detector vector query
components.interface_title: Final reward or detector vector query interface
components.interface:
Return one digit of a reward or detector vector in $[0,1]$, with no port or motion mode. The effective task and seed fix one real value for all digit places. Inactive/source-failed inputs return the canonical zero stream.

\textbf{State and cost.} One fixed clipping continuation and bounded digit; shared seed, cursor and shared mutable registers are not copied.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Vector owner, legal budget and canonical all-seed numerical ranges.\par

steps.tex: Reject a nonvector or malformed request with zero; return zero if inactive or source-failed.
For active $W_0$, choose the pure public reward expression; otherwise choose $E=\operatorname{clip}_{[0,1]}(H_1\cdot\mathrm{scalarprefix})$. Set $s=\varnothing,a=\bot$.
Repeat \Invoke{P-NUMSTEP}{E,t,\mathrm{digit},s,a}{s',o}; set $s=s'$.
For a scalar-prefix request call \Invoke{P-SCALARPREFIX}{\mathcal T,1,j}{a}, with the expression's declared scale adapter.
On DONE$(b)$ erase state and return $b$.

components.title: Distribute increments without merging stored values
components.interface_title: Distribute increments without merging stored values interface
components.interface:
$O$ is the ordered old representative list with values; $J$ is the ordered list of new records $(\mathrm{valid},\mathrm{endpoint},\mathrm{increment})$. $z$ is the old default. The policy $\eta$ specifies the endpoint equivalence in \Dref{D-POLICY}. Every record carries its owner, seed and endpoint; comparison labels are constructed here. The result preserves old representatives separately.

\textbf{State and cost.} Logical full lists; \Lpart{P-KEY receives a materialized endpoint and uses only pure scratch.} All class sums are retained; no low-space claim.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Every old record is present; each record supplies its owner, seed and endpoint, and $\eta$ fixes the selected comparison policy.\par

steps.tex: Use $\kappa(v)=v$ as the comparison label in exact mode. \Lpart{In the full configuration use it also if $d>2h_*$. Otherwise, for each record at endpoint $v$, \Invoke{P-KEY}{\rho,v,b}{\kappa(v)}, with the invoking owner\textquotesingle s block $b$ and seed $\rho$.}
For each comparison label $k$ occurring in $O$ or a valid member of $J$, set $v_k=(0,0)$.
Scan all valid $j\in J$ and add its increment to $v_{\kappa(j)}$, including zero increments.
For every $o\in O$, output the same representative with value $O(o)+v_{\kappa(o)}$.
For a class with no old representative, output its first valid new record with value $(z,0)+v_k$.
All other real endpoints receive default $(z,0)$; return the ordered represented row $W$.

components.title: Choose representatives without losing arrivals
components.interface_title: Choose representatives without losing arrivals interface
components.interface:
Return whether pool code $c$ is an old representative or the first valid new record in a equivalence class without an earlier record. Old representatives are kept separately even when the policy identifies their endpoints. This test does not decide whether a new arrival is added numerically.

\textbf{State and cost.} Candidate, scan index and finite flag use $O(d)$ bits. Old calls increase slack to $2d$ and are suppressed at the top.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Fixed pool order and comparison policy.\par

steps.tex: For an old code, return zero at the top; otherwise \Invoke{P-RAWNUM}{\mathcal T[2d],p,\mathrm{presence},0}{b} and return $b$.
For a new code, \Invoke{P-VALID}{\mathcal T,c}{v}; if $v=0$, return zero.
Set $b=1$. For each earlier pool code $h<c$, \Invoke{P-MATCH}{\mathcal T,c,h}{v}; if $v=1$ set $b=0$.
Finish the entire scan and return $b$.

components.title: Sum all new increments for one representative
components.interface_title: Sum all new increments for one representative interface
components.interface:
Return a coordinate or size digit of the intermediate row at pool code $c$, normalized by $H_d$. A nonrepresentative has old default in coordinate one and zero in coordinate two. A new representative starts at the old default. Only new arrivals are grouped by the selected equivalence.

\textbf{State and cost.} One representative code, one arrival frontier $O(d)$, numerical state and bounded match/digit data. Old-to-new scale shift is charged in the child place; no full old value is stored.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Complete pool code; \Dref{D-RECIPES} gives list length, scale and guard for the full sum.\par

steps.tex: \Invoke{P-REPRESENTATIVE}{\mathcal T,c}{v}; choose the coordinate/size expression $E$ with the appropriate default branch.
Start $s=\varnothing,a=\bot$; repeat \Invoke{P-NUMSTEP}{E,t,\mathrm{digit},s,a}{s',o}; set $s=s'$.
For an OLD request use zero at the top; otherwise \Invoke{P-RAWNUM}{\mathcal T[2d],p_{\rm old},\mathrm{coordinate\ or\ default},j+\lambda d}{a}, with the explicit scale adapter in $E$.
For a NEW$(h,j)$ request, \Invoke{P-MATCH}{\mathcal T,c,h}{u}; if $u=1$, \Invoke{P-ARRIVAL}{\mathcal T,h,\nu,j}{a}; otherwise set $a=0$.
There is one NEW operand for every new code, whether or not it is representative. Never request another old representative's value.
On DONE$(b)$ erase the state and return $b$.

components.title: Compress one completed increment group
components.interface_title: Compress one completed increment group interface
components.interface:
$W$ is the complete represented row after grouping, including a canonical expression for each coordinate and the old-default expression $z$. Return the clipped row, new default, and the fixed selected representative list. Only present candidate representatives are tested, in pool-code order. The canonical expression trees must retain the same padded lists and tie orders as the physical expressions. Each returned representative in $O^+$ carries its new value from $C$ and the matching canonical expression, for the next L-GROUP call.

\textbf{State and cost.} Full arrays and expression trees. Finite candidate scan; no physical resource claim.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} \Dref{D-RECIPES} ranges; $n_d=2^{c_2d}$ and $H_d=2^{\lambda d}$.\par

steps.tex: Set $M_y=\max(|W_y^1|,|W_y^2|)$; \Invoke{L-RANK}{(M_y),n_d,z}{r}; \Invoke{L-RANK}{(W_y^1),k_{\rm row},z}{s}.
Set $u=\max(z,2^{-c_1d},r)$, $q=\max(0,s)$ and $z'=\max(u,\min(q,3u))$.

For each real endpoint and $
u=1,2$, let $b=(z',0)$ and set $C_y^
u=\operatorname{clip}_{[-R_d,R_d]}(b_
u+\operatorname{clip}_{[-7(M_y-2u)_+,7(M_y-2u)_+]}(W_y^
u-b_
u))$.
For each candidate in pool order, put $p=(\lambda+c_1)d+8$; \Invoke{L-CERT}{E_{M_y/H_d},p}{U}; \Invoke{L-CERT}{E_{u/H_d},p}{V}.
Append this candidate to $O^+$ iff $2U-3V>0$. Return $(C,\min(z',R_d),O^+)$.

components.title: Rank the row before compression
components.interface_title: Rank the row before compression interface
components.interface:
Return a digit of the magnitude rank $n_d$ or first-coordinate rank $k_{\rm row}$, at scale $H_d$. The numerical list has one slot per pool code plus $k$ copies of the old default. Nonrepresentatives also supply that default. These added operands are not graph ports.

\textbf{State and cost.} Rank/list indices $O(d)$ plus numerical continuation; default and real operand phases share the same scratch. Old prefix is never called at the top.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} All nondefault intermediate values are represented; nonnegative old default.\par

steps.tex: Choose $k=n_d$ for magnitude or $k=k_{\rm row}$ for coordinate one; start the rank expression state $s$. Set $s=\varnothing,a=\bot$.
Repeat \Invoke{P-NUMSTEP}{E_{\rm rank},t,\mathrm{digit},s,a}{s',o}; set $s=s'$.
For a pool REQUEST$(c,j)$, \Invoke{P-REPRESENTATIVE}{\mathcal T,c}{v}; if $v=1$, \Invoke{P-MERGE}{\mathcal T,c,\mathrm{kind},j}{a}.
For a nonrepresentative or padding request use zero at the top, otherwise \Invoke{P-RAWNUM}{\mathcal T[2d],0,\mathrm{default},j+\lambda d}{a} through the explicit scale adapter.
On DONE$(b)$ erase the state and return $b$.

components.title: Compute the two compression thresholds
components.interface_title: Compute the two compression thresholds interface
components.interface:
Return a normalized digit of $u=\max(z,2^{-c_1d},\operatorname{rank}_{n_d}M)$ or $q=\max(0,\operatorname{rank}_{k_{\rm row}}W^1)$. The first argument wins a numerical tie. Old values are adapted from scale $H_{2d}$ to $H_d$.

\textbf{State and cost.} Finite kind, arithmetic path and the current child request; no entire rank or threshold is stored. Scale shifts contribute to $j-t$.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Raw-sum range and legal dyadic slack.\par

steps.tex: Start the literal $u$ or $q$ expression in the empty numerical state. Set $s=\varnothing,a=\bot$.
Repeat \Invoke{P-NUMSTEP}{E_{\mathrm{kind}},t,\mathrm{digit},s,a}{s',o}; set $s=s'$.
For a rank request call \Invoke{P-INTERMEDIATERANK}{\mathcal T,\mathrm{size\ or\ first},j}{a}.
For old default use zero at the top; otherwise \Invoke{P-RAWNUM}{\mathcal T[2d],0,\mathrm{default},j+\lambda d}{a} with the declared adapter.
The floor $2^{-c_1d}/H_d$ is a public dyadic leaf. On DONE$(b)$ return $b$ after erasing state.

components.title: One compressed coordinate as a digit stream
components.interface_title: One compressed coordinate as a digit stream interface
components.interface:
Return one digit of the compressed coordinate at code $c$, or the new default when $c$ is not representative. The center inside the clipping formula is the unclamped $z'=\max(u,\min(q,3u))$; only the final coordinate and default are clamped to $R_d$.

\textbf{State and cost.} Code $O(d)$, coordinate tag and fixed numerical continuation; no old/default/threshold word survives a child query.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} All-seed ranges for raw sum and compression; valid coordinate.\par

steps.tex: \Invoke{P-REPRESENTATIVE}{\mathcal T,c}{v}; select the coordinate expression when $v=1$, otherwise the default expression.
Start $s=\varnothing,a=\bot$ and repeat \Invoke{P-NUMSTEP}{E_{\rm compression},t,\mathrm{digit},s,a}{s',o}; set $s=s'$.
For $W^\nu$ or size requests use \Invoke{P-MERGE}{\mathcal T,c,\mathrm{coordinate\ or\ size},j}{a}.
For threshold requests use \Invoke{P-THRESHOLD}{\mathcal T,\mathrm{u\ or\ q},j}{a}.

The expression computes $b_
u+\operatorname{clip}_{[-7(M-2u)_+,7(M-2u)_+]}(W^
u-b_
u)$ at common scale $8H_d$, then clamps and adapts to $H_d$.
On DONE$(b)$ erase the state and return $b$.

components.title: Regenerate a retained code one bit at a time
components.interface_title: Regenerate a retained code one bit at a time interface
components.interface:
Return presence of retained ordinal $p<n_d$, or bit $i$ of its selected pool code. The selector uses one fixed finite test independent of later value precision. A missing ordinal returns zero. The caller must reserve the entire returned code before asking for any bit.

\textbf{State and cost.} Two $O(d)$ indices, inclusive count, fixed-place loop markers, one pending digit and a bounded sign. The full selected code is owned by the caller, not hidden here.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Fixed canonical streams and selector margin hypotheses; $0\le p<n_d$.\par

steps.tex: Set passing count $h=0$, found bit $b=0$, and fixed place $P=(\lambda+c_1)d+8$.
For each pool code $c$ in order, \Invoke{P-REPRESENTATIVE}{\mathcal T,c}{v}; skip its numerical test only when $v=0$.

For a representative set $z=0$. For $j=0,\ldots,P$, call \Invoke{P-MERGE}{\mathcal T,c,\mathrm{size},j}{a_j}, then \Invoke{P-THRESHOLD}{\mathcal T,\mathrm{u},j}{b_j}; update $z\gets2z+2a_j-3b_j$, retaining $|z|\le30$ or an absorbing sign $\pm31$.
After all places, pass iff the sign is positive, rejecting equality. If passing and $h=p$, set $b$ to one in presence mode or to code bit $i$ in bit mode. Increment $h$ on every pass.
Finish every pool code and return $b$.

components.title: Row before gating presence, default and coordinate queries
components.interface_title: Row before gating presence, default and coordinate queries interface
components.interface:
Modes are PRESENCE, COORDINATE$(\nu)$ and DEFAULT$(\nu)$. A hole coordinate is zero; DEFAULT is a distinct numerical request. Return one bit or signed digit with no endpoint motion. All zero cells reserved for the selected code count while SELECT is active.

\textbf{State and cost.} Entire reserved code $O(d)$ across selector calls, ordinal and fill frontier, or numerical default state. These branches do not keep each other's work.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Complete raw-prefix request with correct mode-specific fields.\par

steps.tex: Reject invalid slack/mode and inactive tasks with the appropriate zero answer.
For a port mode, reserve and zero its entire $L$-bit code slot. \Invoke{P-SELECT}{\mathcal T,p,\mathrm{presence},0}{v}; if $v=0$, erase the slot and return zero.
In a present port mode only, for $i=0,\ldots,L-1$, \Invoke{P-SELECT}{\mathcal T,p,\mathrm{bit},i}{c_i}; fill the reserved slot. Interpret it only after it is complete.
For COORDINATE, \Invoke{P-COMPRESS}{\mathcal T,c,\nu,t}{b}; erase the slot and return $b$. PRESENCE returns one after erasure.

For DEFAULT set $s=\varnothing,a=\bot$. Drive \Invoke{P-NUMSTEP}{E_{\rm default},t,\mathrm{digit},s,a}{s',o}; answer each threshold request by \Invoke{P-THRESHOLD}{\mathcal T,\mathrm{u\ or\ q},j}{a} until DONE$(b)$, then erase state and return $b$.

components.title: Reference calculation for one hash block
components.interface_title: Reference calculation for one hash block interface
components.interface:
$\mathcal T$ is a complete logical task including the seed and the actual grouping mode. Return its reference result with exact comparisons throughout block $b$, including all structural decisions of same-block descendants. Below block $b$ the actual hash policy remains in force.

\textbf{State and cost.} Idealized full computation. The policy is fixed for the call; lower budgets provide termination.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} $b=\lfloor m(\mathcal T)/h_*\rfloor$.\par

steps.tex: Set a policy $\eta$ that uses exact names at budgets in block $b$ and the actual rule at lower budgets.
\Invoke{L-ESTIMATE}{\mathcal T,\eta}{R}.
Return $R$, including the representative list and fixed access relations.

components.title: Regenerate parameters in shared scratch
components.interface_title: Regenerate parameters in shared scratch interface
components.interface:
$\mathcal T$ is a completed relative handle into the marked root-to-owner record chain, or its frozen bounded-edit view. Return the requested pure field, validity flag, child schema, coefficient bit, or expression tag. Full tuples exist only in the shared reconstruction buffer. Replay has no estimator, presence or terminal callback.

\textbf{State and cost.} One $O(B)$ shared buffer; only a relative field request is retained by the caller. No scratch crosses an opaque query.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Complete frozen portal; bounded link path and a declared pure field request.\par

steps.tex: Start from the immutable root fields and master seed in one scratch buffer.
Scan the completed marked links from root to $\mathcal T$; reject malformed/partial links before interpreting their fields.
At each sample link, \Invoke{P-WORD}{\sigma,H,w,\mathrm{RAW}}{\sigma',b,\omega}; replace the effective seed by $\sigma'$.
Then \Invoke{P-CHILD}{\mathcal T_{\rm parent},\tau,r,\mathrm{side}}{Q}; replace the requested tuple fields by that child result. Non-sample prefix links change only their stated slack/mode.
For a requested public base scalar, \Invoke{P-BASE}{x,\mathrm{mode},p}{v}; use its pure result. Otherwise select the requested bit/field of the reconstructed tuple or literal expression.
Return $r$ and erase the reconstruction buffer; read every link through the supplied virtual view.

components.title: Check a candidate before outer wrap tests
components.interface_title: Check a candidate before outer wrap tests interface
components.interface:
Return whether the descriptor has an intrinsic port, before its outer hit/wrap checks. The cursor and shared mutable registers restore on both answers. Scalar detector and direct-reward records are present after their local checks even when their numerical value is zero.

\textbf{State and cost.} Complete descriptor $O(d)$, finite case, stable LEFT handle and actual bounded token; no old source address. All replay scratch is erased before motion.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Completed descriptor and restoration-safe child portals.\par

steps.tex: \Invoke{P-REPLAY}{\mathcal T,\mathrm{children},c}{Q}; reject INVALID and nonbase zero-budget records.
For Base, \Invoke{P-BASE}{x,\mathrm{presence},Q.p}{b}; return $b$.
For direct, signal, subtraction or copy, remove the known source copy symbol if needed; \Invoke{T-FINAL}{Q.\mathcal T,Q.p,\mathrm{presence},\bot}{b,\bot}; restore that symbol and return $b$.
For a product, \Invoke{P-CAP}{Q.L,Q.p_1,\mathrm{forward}}{b,r}; on failure return zero.
At the midpoint, \Invoke{T-FINAL}{Q.R,Q.p_2,\mathrm{presence},\bot}{v,\bot}; then \Invoke{P-CAP}{Q.L,r,\mathrm{inverse}}{b',p'} and return $v$.
For detector/direct reward return one; for product reward use the same left forward/inverse pair without testing the right vector's value.

components.title: Terminal schedules for primitive paths
components.interface_title: Terminal schedules for primitive paths interface
components.interface:
Return or consume the intrinsic terminal trace of one descriptor. The trace records the family case, known copy symbols, and actual tokens, never the old source address. Scalar families reject endpoint modes. Product success owns one left token and one right trace.

\textbf{State and cost.} $O(d)$ descriptor, finite family/copy tags, one bounded left token and one right trace. The actual source vertex is never retained.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Both directions of every pair are validated before motion; common right tuple independent of old source. RETURN/DISCARD enter their trace branch directly, skipping fresh-request steps.\par

steps.tex: \Invoke{P-REPLAY}{\mathcal T,\mathrm{terminal\ children},c}{Q}; reject invalid/zero-budget cases.
Base fresh request: \Invoke{P-BASE}{x,\mathrm{forward},Q.p}{z}; unpack $z=(b,r)$. Base RETURN: \Invoke{P-BASE}{x,\mathrm{inverse},r}{z}; unpack $z=(b,p\prime)$. DISCARD erases $r$ at the endpoint.
Direct/signal/subtraction: \Invoke{T-FINAL}{Q.\mathcal T,Q.p,\mathrm{retain},\bot}{b,\tau_1}. For cleanup $M$, call \Invoke{T-FINAL}{Q.\mathcal T,Q.p,M,\tau_1}{b,\bot}.

Copy: remove known $\alpha$; \Invoke{T-FINAL}{Q.\mathcal T,Q.p,\mathrm{retain},\bot}{b,\tau_1}; append $\beta$ on success, otherwise restore $\alpha$. RETURN removes $\beta$, calls \Invoke{T-FINAL}{Q.\mathcal T,Q.p,\mathrm{return},\tau_1}{b,\bot}, then appends $\alpha$. DISCARD calls \Invoke{T-FINAL}{Q.\mathcal T,Q.p,\mathrm{discard},\tau_1}{b,\bot} at the endpoint.
Product: \Invoke{P-CAP}{Q.L,Q.p_1,\mathrm{forward}}{b,r}; on success \Invoke{T-FINAL}{Q.R,Q.p_2,\mathrm{presence},\bot}{v,\bot}; then \Invoke{P-CAP}{Q.L,r,\mathrm{inverse}}{b',p'}.

After successful reconnaissance, \Invoke{P-CAP}{Q.L,Q.p_1,\mathrm{forward}}{b,r}; \Invoke{T-FINAL}{Q.R,Q.p_2,\mathrm{retain},\bot}{v,\tau_2}. Failure or RETURN calls \Invoke{T-FINAL}{Q.R,Q.p_2,\mathrm{return},\tau_2}{v\prime,\bot} if a trace exists, erases its link, then \Invoke{P-CAP}{Q.L,r,\mathrm{inverse}}{b\prime,p\prime}.
