DISCARD calls \Invoke{T-FINAL}{Q.R,Q.p_2,\mathrm{discard},\tau_2}{v\prime,\bot} and erases the left token.
STEP's exact finite edits and restoration-safe portals remain U-CATALOG.

components.title: Terminal program for a validated descriptor
components.interface_title: Terminal program for a validated descriptor interface
components.interface:
This terminal adds original-owner validity to intrinsic motion. It returns the same endpoint as the intrinsic descriptor, even for numerical value zero. RETURN and DISCARD use the recorded intrinsic trace; they do not rerun a destination-dependent validity test at the wrong cursor.

\textbf{State and cost.} Complete relative descriptor, entry mode and one terminal-child link. Validation work is erased before delegation.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Valid owner kind; scalar families reject terminal modes. RETURN/DISCARD enter their trace branch directly, skipping fresh-request steps.\par

steps.tex: For a fresh request, \Invoke{P-VALID}{\mathcal T,c}{v}; if $v=0$, fail restoring.
Erase validation-only fields, then \Invoke{T-INTRINSIC}{\mathcal T,c,\mathrm{retain},\bot}{b,\tau_1}.
RETAIN returns that owned trace/link. PRESENCE calls \Invoke{T-INTRINSIC}{\mathcal T,c,\mathrm{return},\tau_1}{b',\bot} before returning the presence bit.
RETURN calls \Invoke{T-INTRINSIC}{\mathcal T,c,\mathrm{return},\tau}{b',\bot}; DISCARD calls \Invoke{T-INTRINSIC}{\mathcal T,c,\mathrm{discard},\tau}{b',\bot}. Erase the parent link after the child.
STEP: the public schedule has no further target, but its phase/slot edit list remains U-CATALOG.

components.title: Terminal program for a raw-row port
components.interface_title: Terminal program for a raw-row port interface
components.interface:
Public modes are PRESENCE, RETAIN, RETURN and DISCARD. RETAIN moves to a raw port endpoint and returns its owned trace; RETURN consumes that trace and restores; DISCARD consumes it at the endpoint. Failure restores with no trace. STEP is a separate proposed graph-transition mode whose missing label/slot catalogue is U-CATALOG.

\textbf{State and cost.} Full reserved code $O(d)$ while selecting, then selected relative code and one terminal link/trace. No opaque child work is copied into the raw graph state.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Complete raw request; trace mode and token must match their originating terminal. RETURN/DISCARD enter their trace branch directly, skipping fresh-request steps.\par

steps.tex: \Invoke{P-REPLAY}{\mathcal T,\mathrm{terminal\ request},(p,\mathrm{mode})}{Q}; reject malformed complete requests.

For a fresh visit reserve the entire selected-code slot. \Invoke{P-SELECT}{\mathcal T,p,\mathrm{presence},0}{b}; if absent erase it and fail. For each bit $i$, \Invoke{P-SELECT}{\mathcal T,p,\mathrm{bit},i}{c_i}.

After the code is complete erase selector-only fields. For old code call \Invoke{T-RAW}{\mathcal T[2d],p_{\rm old},\mathrm{retain},\bot}{b,\tau_1}; for new code call \Invoke{T-DESCRIPTOR}{\mathcal T,c,\mathrm{retain},\bot}{b,\tau_1}.

RETAIN returns $(1,\tau_1)$ with the parent link. For PRESENCE on an old code, \Invoke{T-RAW}{\mathcal T[2d],p_{\rm old},\mathrm{return},\tau_1}{b\prime,\bot}; on a new code, \Invoke{T-DESCRIPTOR}{\mathcal T,c,\mathrm{return},\tau_1}{b\prime,\bot}. Erase the link and return the presence bit.

For cleanup mode $M\in\{\mathrm{return},\mathrm{discard}\}$, read the trace\textquotesingle s old/new tag. Call \Invoke{T-RAW}{\mathcal T[2d],p_{\rm old},M,\tau_1}{b,\bot} or \Invoke{T-DESCRIPTOR}{\mathcal T,c,M,\tau_1}{b,\bot}, respectively, before erasing the parent link. A failed fresh child has no trace; erase its empty link and restore.
STEP: U-CATALOG must supply the finite labels, slot shapes and bounded edits for exactly these phases. No completed STEP implementation is claimed here.

components.title: Final table presence and terminal access
components.interface_title: Final table presence and terminal access interface
components.interface:
Public terminal access to a final row. Dense rows use raw traces; corrections use the whole-column cap's actual paired token. No numerical row value is evaluated here. A vector or invalid port request fails before motion.

\textbf{State and cost.} Finite row kind/mode and one trace or bounded token; no numerical continuation or saved source. All failed calls restore.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Complete row task, canonical trace and matching mode. RETURN/DISCARD enter their trace branch directly, skipping fresh-request steps.\par

steps.tex: \Invoke{P-REPLAY}{\mathcal T,\mathrm{row\ terminal\ kind},\mathrm{mode}}{Q}.
For a fresh dense request, \Invoke{P-CLASS}{\mathcal T,p,A}{v}; if false fail; otherwise \Invoke{T-RAW}{\mathcal T[1],p,\mathrm{retain},\bot}{b,\tau_1}.
For a fresh correction request, \Invoke{P-CAP}{\mathcal T,p,\mathrm{forward}}{b,r}; record $r$ on success.

PRESENCE: for dense mode \Invoke{T-RAW}{\mathcal T[1],p,\mathrm{return},\tau_1}{b\prime,\bot}; for correction mode \Invoke{P-CAP}{\mathcal T,r,\mathrm{inverse}}{b\prime,p\prime}. RETAIN returns the actual trace/token without another opaque call.

For cleanup mode $M\in\{\mathrm{return},\mathrm{discard}\}$, dense mode calls \Invoke{T-RAW}{\mathcal T[1],p,M,\tau}{b,\bot}. Correction RETURN calls \Invoke{P-CAP}{\mathcal T,r,\mathrm{inverse}}{b,p\prime}; correction DISCARD erases its bounded token at the endpoint. Consume the parent link after its child.
STEP's exact label/slot catalogue remains U-CATALOG; it must preserve this dense/capped distinction.

components.title: Read a name bit or test endpoint membership
components.interface_title: A bounded action at the current endpoint
components.interface:
READ-ID$(i)$ returns bit $i$ of the padded current name (zero outside its public range). HIT$(c,r,s)$ tests channel $c$ at rate $r$ after appending suffix $s$. WRAP$(i)$ tests the specified word variant at this endpoint. The result is bounded, the cursor is unchanged, and pure scratch is erased. These actions make no estimator query. Unknown or malformed actions return zero.
\Lpart{READ-KEY and FLIP-KEY delegate to P-ENDPOINT-KEY. Only FLIP-KEY intentionally changes one shared mutable registers cell.}
components.preamble: \textbf{Input/Output.} D-API-P-ENDPOINT; the action's fields are complete before entry.\par

steps.tex: \Invoke{P-REPLAY}{\mathcal T,\mathrm{action},a}{Q}. Reject malformed action fields locally.
For READ-ID$(i)$, read the requested padded bit at the cursor; return it after erasing pure scratch.
For HIT$(c,r,s)$, \Invoke{P-MEMBER}{Q.\sigma,c,\varphi_s(\mathrm{cursor}),r}{b}; return $b$.
For WRAP$(i)$, \Invoke{P-WORD}{Q.\sigma,Q.H,Q.w_{\le i},\mathrm{TEST}}{\sigma',b,\omega}; erase $\sigma'$ and return $b$.
\Lpart{For READ-KEY or FLIP-KEY, \Invoke{P-ENDPOINT-KEY}{\mathcal T,a}{b}; return $b$.} Otherwise return zero.

components.after: \textbf{Distinct callees:} 3 in exact mode; 4 over both modes.

components.title: Visit one old or new representative and return
components.interface_title: Visit one old or new representative and return interface
components.interface:
$c$ is an old/new pool code at slack $d$. Return presence $b$ and the bounded action answer $v$; on absence return $(0,0)$. Success visits its endpoint, executes only the declared endpoint action, and returns to the original cursor. The terminal trace is consumed on every branch.

\textbf{State and cost.} Pool code $O(d)$, finite mode/action and answer; one child trace under the signed boundary contract. Failure retains no trace.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Completed pool code and bounded endpoint action.\par

steps.tex: Decode the old/new tag and reject holes; old codes are absent at the top group.
For an old code, \Invoke{T-RAW}{\mathcal T[2d],c,\mathrm{retain},\bot}{b,\tau}; for a new code, \Invoke{T-DESCRIPTOR}{\mathcal T,c,\mathrm{retain},\bot}{b,\tau}.
If $b=0$, return $(0,0)$ after the callee's restoring failure.
\Invoke{P-ENDPOINT}{\mathcal T,\alpha}{v}.

For an old code call \Invoke{T-RAW}{\mathcal T[2d],c,\mathrm{return},\tau}{b\prime,\bot}; for a new code call \Invoke{T-DESCRIPTOR}{\mathcal T,c,\mathrm{return},\tau}{b\prime,\bot}. Each consumes its trace and restores the source.
Return $(1,v)$ even when $v=0$.

components.title: Visit an intrinsic candidate for its deferred tests
components.interface_title: Visit an intrinsic candidate for its deferred tests interface
components.interface:
Visit the intrinsic endpoint of a descriptor before its outer owner wrap tests. Return presence and the action bit, restoring the cursor. This is needed because destination wrap validity can be tested only after the destination is known.

\textbf{State and cost.} One $O(d)$ descriptor, finite action and answer, plus the terminal-owned trace. No other query survives or occurs above the trace.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Legal descriptor and a declared original-owner action.\par

steps.tex: \Invoke{T-INTRINSIC}{\mathcal T,c,\mathrm{retain},\bot}{b,\tau}. If $b=0$, return $(0,0)$.
\Invoke{P-ENDPOINT}{\mathcal T,\alpha}{v} at the final endpoint, using the original owner's action.
\Invoke{T-INTRINSIC}{\mathcal T,c,\mathrm{return},\tau}{b',\bot}.
Return $(1,v)$ after the trace and link are erased.

components.title: Visit a final raw-row port and return
components.interface_title: Visit a final raw-row port and return interface
components.interface:
Visit a port of the current raw prefix, execute the bounded action, and return. This interface never silently changes slack to $2d$. Missing ports return $(0,0)$ with no action and no motion.

\textbf{State and cost.} Raw ordinal, finite action and answer plus one counted trace; all temporary fields are erased on return.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Raw-prefix task; action allowed by P-ENDPOINT.\par

steps.tex: \Invoke{T-RAW}{\mathcal T,p,\mathrm{retain},\bot}{b,\tau}. If $b=0$, return $(0,0)$.
\Invoke{P-ENDPOINT}{\mathcal T,\alpha}{v}.
\Invoke{T-RAW}{\mathcal T,p,\mathrm{return},\tau}{b',\bot}.
Return $(1,v)$.

components.title: Compare endpoints under the selected policy
components.interface_title: Matching two described endpoints
components.interface:
The complete task and codes describe two repeatable endpoint visits. An absent endpoint never matches. Exact mode returns equality of the padded injective names and restores the cursor. Its live comparison state consists of two relative codes, one $O(\log B)$ position counter, one pending bit and finite flags. These costs count in \Dref{D-RESOURCE}. The policy is fixed before the call.
\Lpart{The full mode uses the exact branch when $d>2h_*$ and P-MATCH-HASH otherwise. It returns the policy's equality, which need not be endpoint equality.}
components.preamble: \textbf{Input/Output.} D-API-P-MATCH. Requires repeatable restoring visits, including absent codes.\par

steps.tex: \Invoke{P-REPLAY}{\mathcal T,\mathrm{comparison},0}{Q}. Read the prescribed comparison mode and padded name length $L_{\rm id}$; erase the reconstruction buffer.
\textit{L only:} If the full policy selects the short comparison, \Invoke{P-MATCH-HASH}{\mathcal T,c_1,c_2}{b} and return $b$.
Set $b=1$. For $i=0,\ldots,L_{\rm id}-1$, call \Invoke{P-VISITPOOL}{\mathcal T,c_1,\mathrm{READ\!\!\!-ID}(i)}{u,x}, then \Invoke{P-VISITPOOL}{\mathcal T,c_2,\mathrm{READ\!\!\!-ID}(i)}{v,y}.
Set $b\gets b\wedge u\wedge v\wedge(x=y)$; erase $x,y,u,v$ before the next position. Finish the loop even after a mismatch.
Return $b$ at the starting cursor.

components.after: \textbf{Distinct callees:} 2 in exact mode; 3 over both modes.

components.title: Short block key at a presented endpoint
components.interface_title: Short block key at a presented endpoint interface
components.interface:
Return the block-$b$ fingerprint bucket in $\{1,\ldots,B\}$ for the supplied endpoint $v$. The effective fair bits are those in $\rho$; a physical caller presents $v$ through the single cursor. No graph query is made. Unpermitted future block requests return INVALID.

\textbf{State and cost.} $O(\log B)$ arithmetic scratch plus sequential access to endpoint bits; no endpoint copy survives a child because there are no child calls.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Effective block access is allowed by \Dref{D-HASHBLOCKS}; prime existence is X-PRIME.\par

steps.tex: Take the least prime $q_{\rm hash}\in[B^3,2B^3]$, found by bounded integer trial division. Let $\ell=\lceil\log_2q_{\rm hash}\rceil$.
Read the three $\ell$-bit chunks for block $b$, reduce them modulo $q_{\rm hash}$, and call them $R,A,C$.
Scan the $c_{\rm ID}B$ padded name bits by Horner's rule to compute $P_v(R)\pmod q_{\rm hash}$.
Put $z=AP_v(R)+C\pmod q_{\rm hash}$ and return $k=1+\lfloor Bz/q_{\rm hash}\rfloor$.

components.title: Read or toggle one fingerprint cell
components.interface_title: One cell indexed by a recomputed fingerprint
components.interface: The action is READ-KEY or FLIP-KEY, and the owner, effective seed and block are fixed by the complete task. A counted shared array $V\in\{0,1\}^{B}$ is available. READ-KEY returns its indexed bit without mutation. FLIP-KEY toggles that bit and returns zero. Neither action changes the cursor or makes an estimator query; its parent owns the obligation to undo a flip.
components.preamble: \textbf{Input/Output.} D-API-P-ENDPOINT-KEY; invalid actions return zero without mutation.\par

steps.tex: \Invoke{P-REPLAY}{\mathcal T,\mathrm{comparison},0}{Q}. Check the owner block and permitted effective coordinates.
\Invoke{P-KEY}{Q.\rho,\mathrm{cursor},Q.b}{k}. Verify $1\le k\le B$ before indexing.
If $a=\mathrm{READ\!\!\!-KEY}$, set $b=V_k$. If $a=\mathrm{FLIP\!\!\!-KEY}$, set $V_k\gets1-V_k$ and $b=0$. Otherwise set $b=0$.
Erase $Q,k$ and pure scratch; return $b$.

components.title: Compare fingerprints using four restoring visits
components.interface_title: Restoring comparison of two fingerprints
components.interface: The codes have the same owner and effective block key. Endpoint existence, paths and the final comparison answer are independent of the incoming contents of the counted $B$-bit catalyst. A visit may fail, but a repeated visit to the same code has the same presence and endpoint. Every nested call restores the catalyst it receives. Return zero if either endpoint is absent; otherwise return equality of the two fingerprints. Restore both cursor and catalyst.
components.preamble: \textbf{Input/Output.} D-API-P-MATCH-HASH. No branch may use a catalyst read to select a path.\par

steps.tex: \Invoke{P-VISITPOOL}{\mathcal T,c_1,\mathrm{READ\!\!\!-ID}(0)}{u,x}; \Invoke{P-VISITPOOL}{\mathcal T,c_2,\mathrm{READ\!\!\!-ID}(0)}{v,y}. If $u v=0$, return zero without a flip.
\Invoke{P-VISITPOOL}{\mathcal T,c_1,\mathrm{FLIP\!\!\!-KEY}}{u_1,z_1}.
\Invoke{P-VISITPOOL}{\mathcal T,c_2,\mathrm{READ\!\!\!-KEY}}{u_2,z_2}. Retain only $z_2$ and finite phase flags.
\Invoke{P-VISITPOOL}{\mathcal T,c_1,\mathrm{FLIP\!\!\!-KEY}}{u_3,z_3}.
\Invoke{P-VISITPOOL}{\mathcal T,c_2,\mathrm{READ\!\!\!-KEY}}{u_4,z_4}. Return $z_2\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}z_4$ after every visit has unwound.

components.title: Precursor and quantized-score terminal programs
components.interface_title: Precursor and quantized-score terminal programs interface
components.interface:
The graph kind is precursor, incoming-$I$ score, or detector score. A score graph at precision $t$ has sinks $J(y,Q)$ for every $0\le Q\le2^t$, including unrealized scores. The payload is owned by the graph exactly once. The score quantization is the clipped floor of the local signed prefix through $t+8$.

\textbf{State and cost.} One graph-owned $t+1$-bit payload, formed as a suffix; bounded carry, port and finite mode. No wrapper copy of the payload or graph is allowed.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Unit-scale local score in $[0,1]$; common source-independent graph tuple and complete raw terminal. RETURN/DISCARD enter their trace branch directly, skipping fresh-request steps.\par

steps.tex: \Invoke{P-REPLAY}{\mathcal T,\mathrm{score\ graph},\mathrm{mode}}{Q}; \Invoke{P-CLASS}{\mathcal T,p,A_I\text{ for }I\text{, else }A}{v}; reject a fresh invalid initial to the separate failure sink.

For score mode set carry $c=0$ and an empty low suffix. For $j=t+8,t+7,\ldots,0$, \Invoke{P-LOCAL}{\mathcal T,p,\mathrm{score\ kind},j}{a_j}; set $u=c+a_j$, take Euclidean bit $u\bmod2$, and set $c=\lfloor u/2\rfloor$.
Discard bits of weight below $2^{-t}$; retain the remaining low suffix. After the last digit, use the carry/sign and high bit to clamp the integer to $[0,2^t]$. Precursor mode omits this step.
Erase arithmetic work; \Invoke{T-RAW}{\mathcal T[1],p,\mathrm{retain},\bot}{b,\tau_1} as the last opaque action.

RETAIN owns the raw trace and one payload. For cleanup mode $M\in\{\mathrm{return},\mathrm{discard}\}$ call \Invoke{T-RAW}{\mathcal T[1],p,M,\tau_1}{b,\bot} and consume the parent trace. DISCARD leaves only the success sink. Failure retains no score payload.
STEP's exact payload/phase edits and all legal artificial sinks remain U-CATALOG.

components.title: Successor and predecessor access to a terminal program
components.interface_title: Successor and predecessor access to a terminal program interface
components.interface:
$G$ is one frozen raw graph view; $i$ is a finite ordered incidence/certificate token. Modes TEST and CROSS inspect or cross one edge. TEST restores cursor and graph even after a paired candidate is rejected. CROSS repeats the validated transition and commits only its bounded edit after lower work is erased. This interface is conditional on the missing five STEP catalogues.

\textbf{State and cost.} Frozen raw view, bounded virtual edit and restoration portal, plus one disjoint lower arena. All raw copies and locators must fit E-CATALOG/E-STACK; no depth-multiplied copied stack.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Finite STEP catalogues, complete-link validation and all-input local bounds: unresolved U-CATALOG.\par

steps.tex: Construct the candidate predecessor/successor virtual view by the bounded edit encoded by $i$; reject malformed edits or incomplete links by finite scans.

Select the active handler and call exactly one of \Invoke{T-RAW}{\mathcal T,p,\mathrm{STEP},G_i}{b,e}, \Invoke{T-DESCRIPTOR}{\mathcal T,c,\mathrm{STEP},G_i}{b,e}, \Invoke{T-INTRINSIC}{\mathcal T,c,\mathrm{STEP},G_i}{b,e}, \Invoke{T-FINAL}{\mathcal T,p,\mathrm{STEP},G_i}{b,e}, or \Invoke{T-SCORE}{\mathcal T,p,\mathrm{STEP},G_i}{b,e}.
The selected STEP contract must validate both restoration directions before motion, recompute its bounded answer/token, and restore using the actual token on rejection.
Compare every produced field with the frozen target by a finite scan; reject unless the normalized certificate also equals $i$.
TEST returns the bit after restoration. CROSS repeats the same accepted STEP in crossing mode, erases its opaque arena, then installs its bounded edit and returns the opposite incidence.
No candidate may guess an erased word or copy an opaque child stack. Until U-CATALOG is supplied, these are specified obligations, not executable incidence rules.

components.title: Reversible contour around one success halt
components.interface_title: Reversible contour around one success halt interface
components.interface:
$G$ is the current graph/incidence state in the component of one specified success halt, with a sentinel at that halt. Return at the next canonical initial or sentinel in the requested contour direction. The graph state and cursor move together; no initial endpoint copy is retained.

\textbf{State and cost.} One continuously allocated graph state and bounded incidence token; no second destination or graph copy in the wrapper.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Finite deterministic graph, total ordered PROBE access and a genuine halt component.\par

steps.tex: First scan the finite incidence alphabet with \Invoke{P-PROBE}{G,i,\mathrm{TEST}}{b,e}. If no edge exists, return the isolated success sentinel, in either direction. Restore the starting incidence label after this existence scan. For forward motion, scan cyclically from it until the next present incidence.
For forward direction only, \Invoke{P-PROBE}{G,i,\mathrm{CROSS}}{b,e}; update the incidence to its opposite label.

For reverse direction, first \Invoke{P-PROBE}{G,i,\mathrm{CROSS}}{b,e}; update to the opposite label, then scan cyclically backward with \Invoke{P-PROBE}{G,i,\mathrm{TEST}}{b,e} until the previous present incidence.
Repeat until the complete canonical-initial format or the success sentinel is reached. Return that mark; an entry tag with nonempty work fields is not a mark.

components.title: Recover an incoming rank from score contours
components.interface_title: Recover an incoming rank from score contours interface
components.interface:
Return a canonical digit of the zero-padded incoming rank: $k_c$ for incoming-$I$ or $j_{\rm det}$ for a pilot detector. At certificate place $r$, each port is scored by T-SCORE's fixed quantization. The result is the $k$th largest quantized score, padded by zero, with all scores in the uncapped relation counted.

\textbf{State and cost.} One graph-owned score field and cursor, bounded saturated count/direction, four inter-pass bits. The wrapper never copies the graph or completed score.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} All legal score sinks admitted; total TOUR access; uncapped source relation.\par

steps.tex: \Invoke{P-REPLAY}{\mathcal T,\mathrm{incoming\ graph},\mathrm{kind}}{Q}; take its fixed rank $k$.
For certificate places $r=t$ and, if $t>0$, $r=t-1$, initialize one graph-owned payload $q=2^r$ at the success sink and count $c=0$.

At each payload $q$, make a full contour using repeated \Invoke{P-TOUR}{G,\mathrm{forward}}{z}; increment $c$ at canonical initials, saturating at $k$. Finish the contour and return to the same payload/sink.
If $c<k$ and $q>0$, decrement this same payload and repeat. At the first $c=k$, or at zero, record $N_r=q\bmod16$ and erase the graph region.
Return the signed decode of $N_t-2N_{t-1}\pmod{16}$, or $N_0$ at $t=0$.

components.title: Evaluate a canonical certificate in the reference computation
components.interface_title: Evaluate a canonical certificate in the reference computation interface
components.interface:
$E$ is a finite canonical expression tree with the normalized leaf
streams and scales in \Dref{D-RECIPES}. Return the integer $N_t(E)$ defined by
\Dref{D-NUMRECIPES} and the specified score quantization for an incoming
rank. The primitive formulas determine the rounding and ties.

\textbf{State and cost.} Explicit operands, prefixes, and integers.
Evaluation of an operand descends the expression tree. The finite
auxiliary expression for a reciprocal is evaluated above the already
specified operand stream.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Finite acyclic expression tree, normalized leaves, valid ranges.\par

steps.tex:
At a rational leaf return its signed-floor certificate. At an
  incoming-rank leaf, materialize the specified score list. For each
  score tree $E'$ call \Invoke{L-CERT}{E',t+8}{U} and use prefix
  $2^{-(t+8)}U$. Apply the incoming-score rule of \Dref{D-NUMRECIPES} and
  return the rank certificate.

For each operand place required by \Dref{D-NUMRECIPES}, call
  \Invoke{L-CERT}{E',j}{U} on the operand tree $E'$.
  A prefix through $j$ is $2^{-j}U$. If a digit is required and
  $j>0$, call \Invoke{L-CERT}{E',j-1}{V} and use $U-2V$.
  At $j=0$ use $U$.

For a sum, minimum, maximum, clip, scale adapter, product, or padded rank,
  return its displayed finite integer formula on those operands
  with the stated order, scale, and ties.

For a reciprocal, use the prefix at the prescribed earlier
  place to form the two coefficients and the virtual tail stream.
  Evaluate the displayed affine and clipping certificate at
  $t+3$ on that stream. Divide its integer result by eight and take
  the floor. Return the resulting $N_t(E)$.

components.title: Finite-prefix affine arithmetic requests
components.interface_title: Finite-prefix affine arithmetic requests interface
components.interface:
This coroutine implements a declared finite affine sum or continuous piecewise-affine formula $F$ on normalized digit operands. A comparison request has a finite prefix length in $F$ and returns its sign; a certificate request returns $N_t(F)\bmod2^\kappa$. $\kappa$ is a fixed program tag. It emits operand requests but calls no operand.

\textbf{State and cost.} Comparison: fixed coefficient/branch tags, bounded accumulator, one pending digit and $T-j+1$ markers. Residue: $H+\kappa=O(d)$ bits and $O(d)$ list indices. These phases do not coexist.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} \Dref{D-RECIPES} normalized ranges; finite coefficient bounds and tie rules; complete resume state. Affine coefficients have the declared common dyadic denominator removed, so the residue-loop $c_i$ are integers.\par

steps.tex: On START check the expression kind, finite list bounds, ranges and guard. For an affine sum set $A=\sum_i|c_i|$, $h=\lceil\log_2(96A)\rceil+1$, $T=\max(0,t-e+h)$ and $H=T+e-t$; zero coefficients return zero.

For each finite-prefix branch comparison set $z=0$. For $j=0,\ldots,T$, set $u=0$; for each operand $i$, emit \Need{i}{j}{b_i} and add $c_i b_i$ to $u$. Update $z\gets2z+u$, storing it up to the declared coefficient-bound threshold and then its absorbing sign. Finish all places and choose the stated tie branch.
Erase comparison markers. For the selected affine form set residue $R=0$ modulo $2^{H+\kappa}$.
For each operand and $j=\max(0,T-H-\kappa+1),\ldots,T$, \Need{i}{j}{b}; set $R\gets R+c_i b2^{T-j}\pmod{2^{H+\kappa}}$.
Return DONE$(\lfloor R/2^H\rfloor\bmod2^\kappa)$. A finite comparison returns DONE$(\operatorname{sign}z)$ after its comparison phase.

components.title: Product-band arithmetic requests
components.interface_title: Product-band arithmetic requests interface
components.interface:
$F$ names two normalized operands $x,y$. Return a certificate residue for $xy$ through the exact band recurrence in \Dref{D-NUMRECIPES}. The state carries the band continuation, finite loop position, residues and at most one pending digit. Operand requests are returned to the client, not executed here.

\textbf{State and cost.} Band residues and saved band continuations total $O(\delta+1)$ at a band-$\delta$ request, plus origin-restoration markers and one digit. Query-free work is $O(t+1)$; no full convolution is stored.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} $x,y\in[-1,1]$, fixed modulus tag and normalized output.\par

steps.tex: Set $h_0=16$ and $h_\delta=16+\lfloor\delta/4\rfloor$. List band $0$ and dyadic $\delta\le4(t+16)/7$.
Process bands from largest to smallest. In band $\delta$, initialize its residue with the already completed larger-band residue shifted down by $h_{\delta^+}-h_\delta$ using signed floor.
Enumerate $k=0$ for band zero, or $\delta\le k<2\delta$ otherwise, and $a=0,\ldots,\kappa+h_\delta-1$; set $u=t-\kappa+1+a$ and skip $u<2k$.
For pair $(i,j)=(k,u-k)$ and also $(u-k,k)$ when $u>2k$, \Need{x}{i}{b}; \Need{y}{j}{c}; add $bc2^{\kappa+h_\delta-1-a}$ modulo $2^{\kappa+h_\delta}$.
After band zero, return DONE$(\lfloor R_0/2^{16}\rfloor\bmod2^\kappa)$.

components.title: Early-prefix reciprocal requests
components.interface_title: Early-prefix reciprocal requests interface
components.interface:
$F$ names $x\in[a,b]\subset(0,1]$. Return a certificate residue for $1/(Cx)$, where the fixed power of two $C\ge\max(1,2/a,4/a^2)$ is part of the expression. The originating $t$ is captured for the entire call. The outer client later undoes $C$ only with a justified scale adapter.

\textbf{State and cost.} Captured origin, fixed arithmetic path and four residue bits; coefficient rebuild words $O(t)$ occur only at early requests. The coroutine retains all active primitive states and counts them.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Fixed positive interval and guards; \Dref{D-NUMRECIPES} projection scales and bounded reciprocal depth.\par

steps.tex: Fix $k=\lfloor t/2\rfloor+c_r$. A coefficient request rebuilds $X=\sum_{j=0}^k x_j2^{k-j}$ using \Need{x}{j}{x_j}; keep this prefix only during that request.

For coefficient digits use exact rational division for $\alpha=2^k/(CX)$ and $\beta=-2^{2k}/(CX^2)$, including the signed-floor remainder rule. Erase prefix, square, denominator and division words after returning the coefficient digit.
The tail operand returns zero for $j\le k$ and otherwise emits \Need{x}{j}{x_j}; it retains no coefficient word.

Drive \Invoke{P-AFFINE}{\operatorname{clip}_{[0,1]}(\alpha+v),t+3,\kappa+3,s_2,a_2}{s\prime_2,o_2}. For its $v=\beta e$ digit request at $j$, drive \Invoke{P-MULTIPLY}{(\beta,e),j,4,s_1,a_1}{s\prime_1,o_1} and, if $j>0$, \Invoke{P-MULTIPLY}{(\beta,e),j-1,4,s_0,a_0}{s\prime_0,o_0}; decode the difference of completed residues. Service their coefficient/tail requests by steps 1--3. New states start empty, answers $\bot$; retain the originating $t$.
If their inner certificate is $R$, return DONE$(\lfloor R/8\rfloor\bmod2^\kappa)$; otherwise return the pending external request and the complete state.

components.title: Finite-prefix order-statistic requests
components.interface_title: Finite-prefix order-statistic requests interface
components.interface:
$F$ gives list length $Q\le2^{Cd}$, rank $k$, and explicit numerical padding/default operands. Return a certificate residue for its largest-first rank. Invalid ranks return the declared default before requesting an operand. A hole contributes its specified default, never an endpoint.

\textbf{State and cost.} Candidate, competitor, rank and count each $O(d)$, one pending digit and signed remaining-place markers. Only selected index and fixed residue survive the last phase.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Complete fixed list semantics and normalized common scale.\par

steps.tex: Set $T=t+8$. For each candidate $i=0,\ldots,Q-1$, initialize $c=0$.
For each competitor $j$, run \Invoke{P-AFFINE}{\mathrm{compare}(i,j,T),0,\kappa,s_1,a_1}{s'_1,o_1}, forwarding each digit request to the client and binding its answer.
Increment $c$ when the complete prefix of $j$ is larger, or equal with $j<i$.
Select the unique $i$ with $c=k-1$; finish finite loops, then erase competitor and count fields.
Accumulate only the last $\kappa+8$ digits of candidate $i$ through $T$ using \Need{i}{j}{b}; return its floor certificate residue as DONE$(R)$.

components.title: Advance one primitive numerical node
components.interface_title: Advance one primitive numerical node interface
components.interface:
$F$ is one normalized primitive node with its direct operands treated as named leaves. Return its complete primitive state and REQUEST or DONE result. This finite arithmetic dispatch does not evaluate a child expression or invoke an external leaf.

\textbf{State and cost.} Finite tag and the one selected primitive state; no additional numerical stack.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} One legal \Dref{D-RECIPES} node, valid normalization and matching state/answer.\par

steps.tex: For affine, min/max, clipping or a scale adapter, \Invoke{P-AFFINE}{F,t,\kappa,s,a}{s^+,o}.
For a product, \Invoke{P-MULTIPLY}{F,t,\kappa,s,a}{s^+,o}.
For reciprocal, \Invoke{P-RECIPROCAL}{F,t,\kappa,s,a}{s^+,o}.
For padded rank, \Invoke{P-RANK}{F,t,\kappa,s,a}{s^+,o}. Return the bound state and result.

components.title: Advance a numerical expression without calling its operands
components.interface_title: Advance a numerical expression without calling its operands interface
components.interface:
$E$ is one of the fixed expressions in \Dref{D-RECIPES} with named operand leaves; mode is DIGIT or CERT$(\kappa)$. START has $s=\varnothing,a=\bot$; a resumed request receives its single bounded answer $a$. Return a complete new state and either REQUEST$(\mathrm{leaf},j)$ or DONE$(b)$. DIGIT returns a signed digit; CERT returns a residue. These are different result types.

\textbf{State and cost.} Complete primitive continuation, expression path, phase and four inter-pass bits belong to the client. No hidden heap or callback stack. Shared public scratch is erased before an external REQUEST.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Closed expression grammar, ranges valid on all seeds, complete resume state and matching answer type.\par

steps.tex: On START obtain the expression tag/scales and public coefficients through \Invoke{P-REPLAY}{E.\mathcal T,\mathrm{expression},E.\mathrm{tag}}{Q}; explicit logical trees already carry these fields.
For a rational leaf, use its declared signed-floor integer division and return its requested residue or digit. Otherwise choose the root node $F$; a new primitive state is empty with answer $\bot$.
Advance the active primitive by \Invoke{P-NODESTEP}{F,t,\kappa,s_F,a_F}{s\prime_F,o_F}. Save the returned state and inspect its request/done tag.

For a strict-subtree digit request $(E\prime,j)$, drive \Invoke{P-NUMSTEP}{E\prime,j,\mathrm{digit},s_c,a_c}{s\prime_c,o_c}. Return any external request to the client and resume from its answer; on child DONE pass its digit to the saved parent primitive. An external leaf is returned directly as REQUEST$(\mathrm{leaf},j)$.

CERT returns the completed residue. DIGIT runs the root certificate passes at $t$ and $t-1$ sequentially, retaining four bits; at $t=0$ run one pass. Decode the difference modulo 16 in $[-8,7]$ and return DONE$(b)$.

components.title: Enumerate exactly the root conditional law
components.interface_title: Enumerate exactly the root conditional law interface
components.interface:
$c$ is the next fixed-length encoding index, initially zero. Return the next admitted seed $\sigma$, its successor index $c^+$, and $b=1$; return $(\bot,\mathrm{end},0)$ when exhausted. Only channel 0 is conditioned at $z_L$. The exact configuration has no auxiliary bits. Every valid encoding is emitted once; any auxiliary bit-string multiplicity is preserved.

\textbf{State and cost.} One $O(B)$ encoding and inclusive frontier; pure scratch erased. The consumer owns the frontier between calls.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} $0\le c\le2^{s(\rho)}$; setup supplies the fixed encoding length.\par

steps.tex: For encoding indices $i=c,\ldots,2^{s(\rho)}-1$, decode three affine channel seeds and the auxiliary bit string declared by $\rho$ (empty in the exact configuration).
Skip out-of-range field coordinates and any zero slope vector.
\Invoke{P-MEMBER}{\sigma,0,z_L,f_L}{b}.
If $b=1$, return $(\sigma,i+1,1)$.
Return $(\bot,2^{s(\rho)},0)$.

components.title: Evaluate one seed on a fixed grid
components.interface_title: Evaluate one seed on a fixed grid interface
components.interface:
Return the clipped numerator of the first ten signed digits of the same root reward estimator, using channel 0, suffix empty, source rate $f_L$, stage $L$ and budget $M$. The seed and task do not change between digit requests.

\textbf{State and cost.} Constant-size digit index and bounded accumulator outside one evaluator call; the $O(B)$ seed/cursor and any declared auxiliary register are shared once.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} $\sigma$ is a valid seed in the setup range; root hit is enforced by SEEDS.\par

steps.tex: Set the cursor to $z_L$; set the integer accumulator $v=0$ and the root vector tuple $\mathcal T=(W_L,0,f_L,\emptyset,M,\sigma)$.
For $j=0,\ldots,9$: \Invoke{P-VECTOR}{\mathcal T,j}{b_j}; set $v\gets v+b_j2^{9-j}$.
Return $a=\min(512,\max(0,v))$.

components.title: Median by repeated finite scans
components.interface_title: Median by repeated finite scans interface
components.interface:
Return the lower median of the multiset of grid numerators returned by TRIAL on the exact SEEDS sequence. Each restart uses frontier zero. No seed or value list is stored.

\textbf{State and cost.} Constantly many $O(B)$ counters plus one seed coexist with one TRIAL call. Iterator, trial scratch and returned stacks are freed on every iteration.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Legal $\rho$ and total trial evaluation on every enumerated seed.\par

steps.tex: Set $n_{\rm trials}=0,c=0$. Repeatedly call \Invoke{P-SEEDS}{\rho,c}{\sigma,c',b}; if $b=0$ stop, otherwise set $c=c'$ and increment $n_{\rm trials}$.
If $n_{\rm trials}=0$, return $0$ (a setup-contract failure branch).
For $a=0,\ldots,512$, set $c=0,v=0$.
Repeat \Invoke{P-SEEDS}{\rho,c}{\sigma,c',b}; stop this scan at $b=0$; otherwise set $c=c'$ and call \Invoke{P-TRIAL}{\rho,\sigma}{u}.
Increment $v$ iff $u\le a$. After the full scan, if $2v\ge n_{\rm trials}$, return $a$.

components.title: One finite estimator, with all structural choices fixed
components.interface_title: One finite estimator, with all structural choices fixed interface
components.interface:
$\mathcal T$ is the complete finite task of \Dref{D-TASKS}; $\eta$ is the selected comparison policy. Return its complete rational values, expression trees, representative lists and fixed access relations. Numerical output precision is absent. For vector tasks the result has no endpoint list.

\textbf{State and cost.} Unlimited finite arrays over seeds and vertices. Recursion on $m$, then finite group/seed/family loops.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Fixed legal parameters, the explicit seed domain and \Dref{D-SLOTS} action; all group costs checked.\par

steps.tex:
Return zero and empty relations if inactive or outside the
  source hit. Return the explicit reward for active $W_0$. Otherwise
  initialize the raw arrays, scalar, and default $z$ to zero and
  set the old list $O=\emptyset$.

For each family and permitted lower budget, call
  \Invoke{L-FAMILY}{\mathcal T,\tau,r,\eta}{F_{\tau,r}}.
  Materialize the result at each effective seed used by its average.

For each family call
  \Invoke{L-AVERAGE}{F_\tau,H_\tau,G,m,c_\tau}{\Delta_\tau,J_\tau}.

For $d=D,D/2,\ldots,1$ perform the update for that group.
  Include the Base term only at $d=D$.
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=1.7em,itemsep=2pt,topsep=3pt]
  \item For rows collect the valid new records in $J_d$ in complete
    code order. Call \Invoke{L-GROUP}{O,J_d,z,d,\eta}{W}, then
    \Invoke{L-COMPRESS}{W,z,d}{C,z,O}.
  \item For vectors add the scalar group increment and clamp to
    $[-R_d,R_d]$.
  \end{enumerate}

For a vector put the final scalar in $C$ with $z=0$ and
  $O=\emptyset$. Call \Invoke{L-ASSEMBLE}{\mathcal T,C,z,O,\eta}{R} and return $R$.

components.title: Deterministic ROBP probability estimator
components.interface_title: Deterministic ROBP probability estimator interface
components.interface:
$x$ is the complete explicitly listed ROBP input. Return the integer numerator $a\in\{0,\ldots,512\}$; the denominator is fixed by the public interface. Malformed input returns zero. The proposed numerical guarantee is \Dref{D-TARGET}; it is not established by this architecture.

\textbf{State and cost.} Root environment, seed counter, one cursor and shared scratch occupy $O(B)$ once. No lower frame owns a second copy.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Fixed constants satisfying E-CONSTANTS, still open.\par

steps.tex: \Invoke{P-SETUP}{x,\eta}{\rho,\mathrm{ok}}. If $\mathrm{ok}=0$, output $0$ and halt.
Initialize the shared registers prescribed by configuration $\eta$; charge their full size once.
\Invoke{P-MEDIAN}{\rho}{a}.
Output $a$ and halt.

components.title: Multiply explicit rational arrays
components.interface_title: Multiply explicit rational arrays interface
components.interface:
$A$ is an explicitly stored $r\times s$ rational array and $B$ an $s\times t$ rational array; a vector is a one-column array. The result has $Z_{ij}=\sum_{k=1}^sA_{ik}B_{kj}$. Empty inner dimension gives the zero array.

\textbf{State and cost.} Input and output arrays plus one rational accumulator; logical resources only.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} Compatible finite dimensions.\par

steps.tex: Allocate an $r\times t$ zero array $Z$.
For $i=1,\ldots,r$ and $j=1,\ldots,t$, set $z=0$.
For $k=1,\ldots,s$, set $z\gets z+A_{ik}B_{kj}$; store $Z_{ij}=z$.
Return $Z$.

components.title: Rank with an explicit padding value
components.interface_title: Rank with an explicit padding value interface
components.interface:
$v$ is a finite ordered rational list, $k\ge1$, and $z$ is the padding value. Return the $k$th largest member of $v$ with $k$ additional copies of $z$. Equal values are ordered by their original list index. Padding is numerical data and never creates a graph port.

\textbf{State and cost.} Explicit list, two indices, count and scalar comparisons; no physical-space claim.
components.preamble: \textbf{Requires.} $k$ is a positive integer.\par

steps.tex: Append $k$ copies of $z$ to $v$, obtaining $v'$.
For each index $i$, set $c=0$ and scan all indices $j$.
Increment $c$ if $v'_j>v'_i$, or if $v'_j=v'_i$ and $j<i$.
If $c=k-1$, return $r=v'_i$.

definitions.title: Explicit binary branching programs
definitions.tex:
An input of length $n$ explicitly lists the layers, vertices, start vertex,
accepting terminal vertices, and two labelled next-vertex indices for every
nonterminal vertex of a binary read-once branching program. Each step consumes
one fresh fair bit and goes to the next layer. Repeated destinations retain their
edge labels. Vertices and edges are listed, not specified by a succinct circuit;
in particular the number of layers is at most the description length. The
zero-layer case is allowed. A malformed description receives output zero and
halts. General rational transition probabilities are outside this root interface.

definitions.title: The estimator output and counted memory
definitions.tex:
The proposed deterministic transducer has an endmarked read-only input and a
write-only output. It outputs an integer $a\in\{0,\ldots,512\}$ denoting $a/512$,
with
\[
 \left|\frac a{512}-\Pr[\text{the given ROBP accepts}]\right|\le\frac1{16}.
\]
It must halt on every input in $O(\log(n+2))$ ordinary work bits. All head positions,
seeds, counters, address words, scratch, catalyst bits, arithmetic states and
retained recursion records count. No separate time bound is asserted. This is a
constant-error probability estimator, sufficient to distinguish the usual
$1/3$ and $2/3$ gap. No variable accuracy parameter is silently free.

definitions.title: The same estimator with additional workspace
definitions.tex: The relaxed target has exactly the input, output, error, invalid-input and halting requirements of \Dref{D-INPUT} and \Dref{D-TARGET}. Its workspace bound is $O(B\log(B+2))$, where $B=\Theta(\log(n+2))$. This is $O(\log n\log\log n)$ for large $n$; the displayed form also covers bounded input lengths. Every bit counted in \Dref{D-TARGET} is still counted.

definitions.title: The base graph and copied vertex names
definitions.tex:
The paired graph of \Aref{P-BASE} has $n_0=O(n+1)$ vertices, transition matrix $S$,
and terminal reward vector $e$. It is forward, substochastic, and has incoming
and outgoing degree at most two. Its exact continuation vector is
$p=(I-S)^{-1}e\in[0,1]^{V_0}$. A stage-$l$ name is a base name followed by $l$
copy labels in $\{0,\ldots,d_0-1\}$; $V_l$ denotes this set and $f_l=16^{-l}$.
Names of different lengths are encoded injectively with a length delimiter.
Appending a fixed suffix is an affine map on its legal name interval.
The field is chosen larger than all names; a suffix is never selected from the seed.

definitions.title: Fixed root parameters and precision ranges
definitions.tex:
Choose
\[
 L=\min\{j\ge0:8^j\ge48n_0\},\quad N=n_0d_0^L,
 \quad 2^{3r}\ge8N48^3,
\]
with the least integer $r\ge1$. Let $B$ be a padded power of two of order
$\log(n+2)$, and take statistical budget $M=c(B+L+r)$. Constants, including
$c,d_0$ and the field exponent, are fixed program constants whose simultaneous
effective selection is \id{E-CONSTANTS}; that assignment remains open.
The requested root digit places are just $0,\ldots,9$, but internal requests
may have place $O(B)$ and must be charged.

definitions.title: Signed-digit streams and root truncation
definitions.tex:
A normalized signed-digit stream has digits in $\{-6,\ldots,6\}$ and value
$\sum_{j\ge0}a_j2^{-j}$. Truncation after place 9 incurs at most
$6\sum_{j=10}^\infty2^{-j}=3/256$. Clipping to $[0,1]$ cannot increase this
error.

definitions.title: The single event used by deterministic enumeration
definitions.tex:
Let $A_\sigma(v)\in[0,1]$ denote the reward returned by the selected logical estimator at stage $L$, and let $w_L(v)$ be its exact hierarchy target. The primary start is $z_L$. The root event is
\[
 H_0=\{X_{f_L}^0(z_L)=1\}.
\]
The required moment premise, for the same seed law, is
\[
 \frac1N\mathbb E_\sigma\sum_{v\in V_L}\frac{X_{f_L}^0(v)}{f_L}
          |A_\sigma(v)-w_L(v)|^3\le2^{-3r}.
\]
Channels 1 and 2 are not conditioned at the root. An algorithm that filters either extra hit requires a different accuracy theorem.

definitions.title: The conditional seed-action interface
definitions.tex:
The abstract input is a finite seed set with an explicitly specified conditional
uniform measure. A condition names at most one fixed endpoint per channel and
may fix a prescribed subset of auxiliary bits. The interface supplies a fixed
constant number of symmetric generator slots, at least half lazy, a transition
and inverse algorithm, a positive spectral gap independent of all size
parameters, and a word description of $O(h)$ bits for length $h$. It must also
supply an endpoint-independent bijective word expansion with exactly one valid
variant per conditioned seed. This last requirement is separate from expansion.
An arbitrary expander on an unconditioned space does not satisfy this interface.

definitions.title: The common probability space
definitions.tex:
A channel seed is $(a_0,a_1)\in\mathbb F_p^4\times(\mathbb F_p^4\setminus\{0\})$, uniform on this finite set. The three channels are independent. For $a=16^{-j}$, set $L_a=\lceil p2^{-j}\rceil$ and
\[
 X_a^c(v)=\mathbf1\{a_0^c+v a_1^c\bmod p\in[0,L_a)^4\},\qquad \pi_a=(L_a/p)^4.
\]
An environment may also contain an independent uniform bit string of a fixed public length. In the exact configuration this length is zero. A task's probability space, including this choice, is fixed independently of its numerical precision and statistical budget. All expectations below refer to that space unless a conditioning event is displayed.

definitions.title: The concrete conditional action spaces
definitions.tex:
At a specified hit endpoint, changing coordinates to $(a_1,w)$ identifies a
conditioned channel with
\[
 (\mathbb F_p^4\setminus\{0\})\times(\mathbb Z/L_a\mathbb Z)^4.
\]
The same integer elementary matrix acts on both factors and translations act on
the second. An unrestricted channel uses endpoint zero and $L=p$.
For the free auxiliary bits, split their number into four $\ell_{\rm aux}$-bit integers and
at most three residual bits. Use the affine action on
$(\mathbb Z/2^{\ell_{\rm aux}}\mathbb Z)^4$ and lazy flips on the residual bits; fixed bits do
not move. The number of factors stays bounded. \Aref{P-SEEDSTEP} is the concrete
candidate; \id{A-ACTION} derives its uniform gap from the two Shalom inputs and
the finite-action argument. \id{A-MIX} applies the explicitly imported finite
interpolation contract. A-ACTION proves the finite-action specialization under the two external contracts. Identifying the same law at each estimator caller remains a separate analytical obligation.

definitions.title: Endpoint-independent word variants
definitions.tex:
For a channel letter $(A,c)$, \Aref{P-WORD} enumerates the bounded wrap choices
$z$ and uses the full-seed map
$(a_1,a_0)\mapsto(Aa_1,Aa_0+c+Lz)\bmod p$.
Its validity test is $0\le Aw+c+Lz<L$ in integer representatives. Exactly one
variant passes. All variants retain the original word weight; there is no
extra wrap normalization. Failed variants contribute zero. A fixed variant is
a full-seed permutation, but an adaptively selected valid variant need not
preserve an unconditional distribution. All probability arguments must retain
the declared condition and its measure.

definitions.title: A concrete constant-size generator alphabet
definitions.tex:
Use 512 equally weighted slots, indexed by a factor in $\{0,\ldots,7\}$ and a
local slot in $\{0,\ldots,63\}$. Factors 0,1,2 are the three channel spaces;
factor 3 is the four-integer free-bit space; factors 4,5,6 are the possible
residual bits; factor 7 is identity. Absent factors are identity.
In factors 0--3, slots 0--31 are identity, 32--55 are $I\pm E_{ij}$ for
$i\ne j$ in lexicographic order, positive before negative, and 56--63 are
translations $\pm e_i$ in coordinate order, positive before negative.
A translation leaves a channel slope unchanged. In each residual-bit factor,
slots 0--31 are identity and slots 32--63 flip the bit. This fixes a symmetric
alphabet with at least half its slots lazy. If there are $4\ell_{\rm aux}+r$ free bits,
$0\le r<4$, factor 3 reads the first four consecutive $\ell_{\rm aux}$-bit blocks as integers
modulo $2^{\ell_{\rm aux}}$; factors 4 onward use the remaining bits. The public fixed-coordinate
mask chooses these positions. A fixed generator acts on no frozen bit.

Channel wraps have coordinates in $\{-1,0,1\}$, zero in unchanged coordinates.
The one valid wrap per channel letter is tested in integer representatives.
Auxiliary factors use their directly invertible modular action and need no
channel wrap guess. A length-$h$ word has weight $512^{-h}$, with no division
by a wrap count. A-ACTION proves the uniform gap for this explicit specialization. It is a theorem about this conditional product action, not about arbitrary conditioned subgraphs.

definitions.title: Endpoint matching and the row that it defines
definitions.tex:
A comparison policy $\eta$ fixes an equivalence relation on endpoint names for each complete task and increment group, independently of requested digits. Exact mode uses equality of the injective names. Let $O$ be the ordered old representatives, $J$ the valid new arrivals and $(z,0)$ the old default. For an equivalence class $C$, put
\[
 v_C=\sum_{j\in J:\,\operatorname{endpoint}(j)\in C}\operatorname{increment}(j).
\]
L-GROUP keeps every $o\in O$ separately with value $O(o)+v_{[o]}$. A class containing no old representative creates its first valid arrival with value $(z,0)+v_C$. All other names retain the default. Compression and later gates use this precise row. No claim about its accuracy is part of this definition.

definitions.title: Padded ranks, holes and logical enumeration
definitions.tex:
A rank is the $k$th largest value. Numerical row ranks are padded by the specified
number of default values; incoming ranks are padded by zeros. A hole is an absent
port, not a default-valued present port. Strict structural tests reject equality.
The representation may retain a coordinate equal to the default.
Logical array multiplication and padded rank computation are explicit calls to
\Aref{L-MATMUL} and \Aref{L-RANK}. Finite expectations enumerate their stated seed
sublist and divide its scalar sum by its count. Physical ranks and averages use
the separately named request and sample procedures. No caller executes a
mathematical definition as though it were a subroutine.

definitions.title: Smooth cutoffs and fixed hierarchy constants
definitions.tex:
For $A<B$, define
\[
 \chi(t)=\begin{cases}0&t\le0,\\10t^3-15t^4+6t^5&0<t<1,\\1&t\ge1,\end{cases}
 \qquad \chi_{A,B}(v)=\chi((v-A)/(B-A)).
\]
The hierarchy uses fixed rational thresholds
$0<\delta_0<\delta_1<\theta_1/100$ and
$0<\theta_1<\theta_2<1/512$, a fixed round count $K$, and
\[
 Q(v)=(v-\theta_1)_+\chi_{\theta_1,\theta_2}(v),\quad
 \phi(v)=\chi_{\delta_0,\delta_1}(v),\quad
 \gamma(v)=1-\chi_{1/2,4/5}(v).
\]
Let $b_Q=K+2$, $k_f=16^{\kappa_f}\ge2(K+1)$, and choose a positive fixed
$\zeta\le\min(1,\theta_1/2,\delta_0/2,1/4)$ satisfying the later compression
inequalities. These symbols are constants, not additional procedures.

definitions.title: Raw coordinates and their local gates
definitions.tex:
A completed raw row is a pair $(v_{xy},v^2_{xy})$ with default $(z_x,0)$.
The superscript 2 labels a coordinate; it is not a square. Let $s_x$ be its
$k_{\rm row}$th first-coordinate rank, with default padding. For the owner's
threshold $\theta$ set
\begin{align*}
h_\theta(v)&=\chi_{\theta/2,3\theta/4}(v),&
R_\theta(s)&=1-\chi_{\theta/1000,\theta/500}(s),\\
I_\theta(v,s)&=\chi_{\theta/8,\theta/4}(v)
 (1-\chi_{\theta/100,\theta/50}(s)),\\
J_\theta(v,s)&=\chi_{41\theta/500,9\theta/100}(v)
 (1-\chi_{13\theta/500,27\theta/1000}(s)).
\end{align*}
The auxiliary $J$ is a smooth witness for analysis, not a new runtime call.
Corrections use $\theta_1$, bins use $1/2$, and scores use $\delta_0$.
The cubic cutoff convention follows Run 3/Run 7. The distinction between cubic and eighth-moment analyses is discussed in the full-space additions.

definitions.title: Bin factors and routed residual factors
definitions.tex:
For $b=16^{-j}$ the bin factor is
\[
 k_b(v)=\begin{cases}
 v_c\chi_{1/2,1}(v_c),\ v_c=\operatorname{clip}_{[0,1]}v,&j=0,\\
 v\chi_{1/2,1}(v)(1-\chi_{1/2,1}(v/16)),&j>0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Correction mains use $k_O(v)=Q(\operatorname{clip}_{[0,b_Q]}v)$.
Transition and unrouted residual mains use $k_a(v)$.
A residual with route $\beta$ multiplies by $s_\beta((a/f_l)v)$ when $a<1$;
when $a=1$ its routing argument is $v_c/f_l$, using the clipped $v_c$.
The functions $s_\beta$ are defined in \Aref{L-SPLIT}.

definitions.title: Preparation, main and score formulas
definitions.tex:
Local preparation is $h_\theta(v)R_\theta(s)$; local main is
$Y_\tau k_O(v)R_\theta(s)/\operatorname{clip}_{[1/2,1]}(v^2/\zeta)$;
score is $\phi(v)R_{\delta_0}(s)$. Corrections multiply by their own incoming
gate $1-\chi_{1/4,1/2}(\operatorname{rank}_{k_c} I)$, and mains also by their
specified detector multiplier. Bins and scores omit incoming gates. Fixed
structural classes cover these supports on every seed, including inaccurate
ones. An overfull correction column is deleted as a whole.

definitions.title: Canonical finite certificates and structural tests
definitions.tex:
Let $\widetilde v_t=2^{-t}N_t$ be the deterministic certificate produced by the
fixed numerical request rules, with $|N_t-2^tv|<2$. Ties, guards and residue
order are fixed once. Logical reference algorithms may generate these finite
certificates with unrestricted arithmetic; physical algorithms must implement
the same rules. A structural test requests its prescribed place once for that
kind, independent of later output precision. This replaces any ambiguous
instruction to decide an exact real sign. The finite selector in \Aref{P-SELECT}
and the class tests in \Aref{P-CLASS} define the representation used here.
Agreement with source floor-prefix conventions is a proposed representation
comparison, not an identity assumed without proof. Every comparison policy uses these same tests.

definitions.title: Finite task records, rates and analytic ranks
definitions.tex:
A row task contains an owner, stage $l$, round/route when applicable, a permutation
$(\mathsf S,\mathsf T,\mathsf M)$ of channel roles, rates $(u;a,\tau)$,
source and destination suffixes $(s,t)$, a budget, and its effective seed.
The current source and destination vertices are arguments, not hidden fields
of the semantic tuple. Legal suffixes satisfy $l+|s|,l+|t|\le L$.
A preparation always has $\tau=a$; a main has $\tau\le a$.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{lX}
\toprule Owner & Allowed rates and extra data\\\midrule
Transition bin & $u\le f_l$, $a\le f_l$; preparation or main.\\
Pilot correction & $u\le f_l$, $a=f_l$, round $1\le i\le K$; preparation or main.\\
Actual correction & Same rate domain and round range.\\
Residual bin & $u\le f_l$, $a\le\min(1,k_ff_l)$; route $\perp$ or a copy label.\\
Pilot score & $u=a=\tau=f_l$, round $1\le i\le K$.\\
Reward vector $W_l$ & One source channel/suffix, rate $u\le f_l$.\\
Detector vector $U_{l,i}$ & One source channel/suffix, intrinsic rate $u=f_l$.\\\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{center}
Every row vanishes outside its source hit and broad destination hit; vectors
vanish outside their source hit. Put
\[
 k_{\max}=L+\left\lceil M/(2k_{\rm prec})+M/(4c_0)\right\rceil+2,
 \qquad\mathcal R=\{16^{-j}:0\le j\le k_{\max}\}.
\]
All rates lie in this finite grid and $p>2^{k_{\max}}$.
For $a=16^{-k_a}$ and $u=16^{-k_u}$, activity requires positive budget $m$ and
\[
 p_{\rm acc}=m/k_{\rm prec}-2k_a-2k_u-a_*i_*>0.
\]
For a vector use broad rate $a=f_l$. Inactive tasks return zero, default zero,
and empty access, making no child calls. With $L_*=6K+6$, the analytic ranks
$i_*$ are $L_*l$ plus these offsets:
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lr@{\qquad}lr}
\toprule
$W_l$&1&Transition prep/main&2,3\\
Score $i$&$4i$&$U_{l,i}$&$4i+1$\\
Pilot prep/main $i$&$4i+2,4i+3$&Actual prep/main $i$&$4K+2i+2,4K+2i+3$\\
Residual prep/main&$6K+4,6K+5$&&\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Local functions of a completed raw row keep its owner's rank. This rank organizes
analytic accuracy; it is not by itself a physical stack bound.

definitions.title: Common child budgets and scale weights
definitions.tex:
Write $\tau_b=\min(a,b)$ and $w_b=(b/a)\pi_a/\pi_{\tau_b}$.
For one lower family budget $r$, all factors share the same transformed seed.
The complete child maps below replace a broad informal ``recursive sample.''
Only the named lower evaluator is a logical call; evaluating the scalar formula
on its results is ordinary exact arithmetic in the logical algorithm.

definitions.title: Row families and their complete child maps
definitions.tex:
Brackets below give roles, source rate, usage rate, source suffix and destination
suffix; a bin name supplies its broad rate. Write $H$ for the indicated pilot
or actual correction. The lower child budget is $r$ in every displayed factor.
\begin{align*}
 T^{\rm dir}_{b,r}(x,y)&=w_b B^C_{l,b,r}
 [\mathsf S,\mathsf T,\mathsf M;u,\tau_b;s,t](x,y),\\
 T^{\rm prod,H,j}_{b,r}(x,y)&=w_b\frac{f_l}{\pi_{f_l}}
 \sum_zX_{f_l}^{\mathsf M}(z)
 H_{l,j,r}[\mathsf S,\mathsf M,\mathsf T;u,f_l;s,\emptyset](x,z)\\
 &\hspace{17mm}\cdot B^C_{l,b,r}
 [\mathsf M,\mathsf T,\mathsf S;f_l,\tau_b;\emptyset,t](z,y),\\
 T^{\rm sub}_r(x,y)&=-w_{f_l}F_{l,K,r}
 [\mathsf S,\mathsf T,\mathsf M;u,\min(a,f_l);s,t](x,y).
\end{align*}
In the product the right tuple contains no old source, old rate $u$, old source
suffix, or left port. It is one common right function at each midpoint.
The left correction has broad and usage rates both $f_l$.
For $l>0$, $x=x_0\alpha$, $y=y_0\beta$, set
\[
 \bar r_{0,r}=1,\quad
 \bar r_{\alpha,r}=\chi_{1/4,1/2}
   (\max_{h\le K}U_{l-1,h,r}[\mathsf S,\alpha s](x_0))\ (\alpha>0),
\]
\[
 T^{\rm copy}_{b,r}(x_0\alpha,y_0\beta)
 =w_b\bar r_{\alpha,r}B^{D,\beta}_{l-1,b,r}
 [\mathsf S,\mathsf T,\mathsf M;u,\tau_b;\alpha s,\beta t](x_0,y_0).
\]
The detector has its intrinsic source rate $f_{l-1}$ and no destination data.
Define $\mathcal B_l^C=\{16^{-j}:l\le j\le k_{\max}\}$ and
$\mathcal B_l^D=\{16^{-j}:\max(0,l-\kappa_f)\le j\le k_{\max}\}$.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{p{.21\textwidth}p{.20\textwidth}X}
\toprule Owner & Exact base at $l=0$ & First-coordinate families\\\midrule
Transition & $S_{xy}/a$ & At $l>0$: copy for $b\in\mathcal B_{l-1}^D$.\\
Pilot prep/main or score $i$ & $S_{xy}$ & At $l>0$: direct over $\mathcal B_l^C$. At $i>1$: product with pilot round $i-1$ over the same scales.\\
Actual prep/main $i$ & $S_{xy}$ & At $l>0$: direct. At $i>1$: product with actual round $i-1$, both over $\mathcal B_l^C$.\\
Residual prep/main & $S_{xy}/a$ & At $l>0$: direct. At every stage: actual round-$K$ products over $\mathcal B_l^C$, and subtraction.\\\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{center}
At positive stages all exact bases are zero. There is no round-zero product.
A residual's route changes its own main factor and preparation identity, not
the routes of product children. Preparations have no second-coordinate family.
Every main has its own preparation signal $\zeta P_r$ with usage changed to $a$,
conditioned at the original narrow destination rate $\tau$, and multiplied by
that original hit. There is no further importance factor in this signal.

definitions.title: Increment groups and their conditional averages
definitions.tex:
For a scale family the cost is $c_b=c_0(1+|\log_2(b/a)|)$; a fixed family costs
$c_0$. Put $D=2^{\lfloor\log_2m\rfloor}$. At groups
$d=D,D/2,\ldots,1$, each first-coordinate increment is its base (only at $D$)
plus the finite sum
\[
 \sum_{\rm families}\sum_{\substack{r\ge1,\ d\le m-r<2d\\c_b\le m-r}}
 \mathcal K_{H_{\rm broad}}^{\ell_{\rm mix}(m-r)}(T_{b,r}-T_{b,r-1}).
\]
Set every family at nonpositive budget to zero. $H_{\rm broad}$ specifies the
source and broad destination hits. The second coordinate uses the identical
formula with the owner's preparation signal, cost $c_0$, and narrow condition
$H_{\rm narrow}$, followed by the original narrow hit. Both signs use the same
word and wrap tests. The aggregate formula expands into the signed records returned by
\Aref{L-AVERAGE}. Each new row record retains its full code. The caller
collects the families and the applicable Base records in that code
order before choosing representatives. New terms are grouped by \Aref{L-GROUP}; every completed
group is compressed by \Aref{L-COMPRESS}. Future increments do not read the
current buffer. This condition is needed for the reverse removal of clamps.

definitions.title: Detector and reward vector families
definitions.tex:
For a detector vector $U_{l,i,m}[c,s](y)$, its one family is the zero-padded
$j_{\rm det}$th rank of
\[
 \{\mathrm{Score}_{l,i,r}[c+1,c,c+2;f_l,f_l;\emptyset,s](x,y):
          X_{f_l}^{c+1}(x)=1\}.
\]
The rank is formed first, then averaged under the sole source hit at $y$.
For a reward $W_{l,m}[c,u,s](x_0\alpha)$ with $l>0$ and $f=f_{l-1}$,
its one family is
\begin{align*}
 \bar r_{\alpha,r}\bigg[W_{l-1,r}[c,u,\alpha s](x_0)
 +\frac f{\pi_f}\sum_zX_f^{c+1}(z)&F_{l-1,K,r}
 [c,c+1,c+2;u,f;\alpha s,\emptyset](x_0,z)\\
 &\cdot W_{l-1,r}[c+1,f,\emptyset](z)\bigg].
\end{align*}
At active stage zero the reward is $e$ exactly. Vectors add scalar groups,
clamp to $[-R_d,R_d]$ after each, and finally clip to $[0,1]$; they have no ports.

definitions.title: Final gates, multipliers and the root task
definitions.tex:
Final correction assembly uses the incoming rank of $I$ from its own raw row.
A pilot main of round $i$ uses
$\gamma(\max_{h\le i}U_{l,h,m-c_{\rm col}}[\mathsf T,t])$;
an actual main uses $h\le K$. These vectors have intrinsic rate $f_l$ and no
old-source data. Final bins use multiplier and incoming gate one. Scores omit
signal, normalizer, cap and multiplier. The physical root uses the reward tuple
$(W_L,c=0,u=f_L,s=\emptyset,m=M)$.

definitions.title: Domains and pointwise bounds for a shared-seed product
definitions.tex:
Fix legal rates $u\le f$ and $b\le f$, integers $k,k_c\ge1$, and the source, midpoint and destination channels. Use one finite name universe, extending tables by zero where necessary, with the same normalization $N$ in every factor norm. On one common seed let $\bar F,F^*$ be nonnegative correction tables at rates $(u,f)$ and $\bar B,B^*$ bin tables at $(f,b)$, all bounded by the fixed final scale $H_*\ge1$. Each left and right row has at most $k$ nonzero entries; the ideal left relation has incoming degree at most $k_c$ on every seed. Every right table is a function of $(z,y,\sigma)$ independent of the old source $x$. Masks are the displayed source/midpoint/destination hits. Put
\[
 V_{xy}=\frac f{\pi_f}\sum_z Z_f(z)\bar F_{xz}\bar B_{zy},\qquad
 V^*_{xy}=\frac f{\pi_f}\sum_z Z_f(z)F^*_{xz}B^*_{zy},
\]
with $f/\pi_f\le1$, and set $d_F=\|\bar F^{1/3}-(F^*)^{1/3}\|_{u,f}$ and $d_B=\|\bar B^{1/3}-(B^*)^{1/3}\|_{f,b}$. The rate-$f$ mask in both factor norms is $Z_f$. These are the weighted norms of \Dref{D-ERROR}; the masks are retained even when errors and supports are correlated.

definitions.title: The weighted cubic error and its allocation
definitions.tex:
For a signed row error $H$ use the normalized cubic quantity
\[
 \|H\|_{u,a}^3=\frac1N\mathbb E_\sigma\sum_x\frac{X_u(x)}u
                    \sum_yY_a(y)|H_{xy}|^3.
\]
For a row statistic or vector omit the destination sum. For bounded nonnegative
row outputs, apply this norm to the difference of their real cube roots.
Raw bias/noise uses the ordinary norm. The allocation on an owner is
$\varepsilon=2^{-p_{\rm acc}}$; constants in the local estimates are independent
of the input, rates and number of scale bins. Dummy default positions are not
counted with the multiplicity of the ambient vertex universe.

definitions.title: Complete relative arrival codes
definitions.tex:
At dyadic slack $d$, a code has these fields in this order: $h$ in $d$ bits;
a signed-magnitude scale offset in $d+1$ bits; one sign bit $\epsilon$;
a four-bit family tag; copy symbols $\alpha,\beta$ of
$a_0=\lceil\log_2d_0\rceil$ bits each; two $c_2$-bit ports; and
$2\ell_{\rm mix}d$ word slots, each with nine letter bits and eight wrap bits.
Unused fields and slots are zero. Negative zero and wrap code 11 are invalid;
00,01,10 represent $0,1,-1$. A sufficient fixed width is
$C_{\rm desc}d$, with $C_{\rm desc}=34\ell_{\rm mix}+8+2a_0+2c_2$.

Tags 0--8 are Base, direct, product, subtraction, copy, signal, detector,
direct reward and product reward. A nonbase code has $d\le h<2d$,
$r=m-h\ge1$, child budget $\mu=r-\epsilon\ge0$, and uses only its first
$\ell_{\rm mix}h$ word slots. For scale families $b=a16^e$ and
$c_0(1+4|e|)\le h$; fixed families have $e=0,c_0\le h$.
Base is legal only at $l=0,d=D$ with one labelled base port and all other fields
zero. Direct/subtraction/signal use one port; product uses two; copy uses the
copy symbols and one port; detector uses no port; direct reward uses $\alpha$;
product reward uses $\alpha$ and one port. The owner/tag compatibility is exactly
the complete family dispatch in \Dref{D-ROWFAMILIES}. Zero budget contributes zero without
a child; it is not a new seed experiment.

definitions.title: Returned child fields
definitions.tex:
Write a row tuple as
$(O,l,i,\beta;\mathsf S,\mathsf T,\mathsf M;u,a,\tau;s,t;r,\sigma)$,
omitting irrelevant round/route fields. P-CHILD returns the following fields;
unmentioned semantic fields are inherited only when this table says so.
All listed children share the supplied transformed seed $\sigma$ and budget $r$.
\begin{longtable}{p{.15\textwidth}p{.78\textwidth}}
\toprule Family & Returned children and coefficient\\\midrule\endhead
Direct & Transition main at $(l,b)$, roles unchanged, rates $(u,b,\min(a,b))$, suffixes $(s,t)$; coefficient $w_b$.\\
Product & LEFT: pilot/actual main at the selected round, roles $(\mathsf S,\mathsf M,\mathsf T)$, rates $(u,f_l,f_l)$, suffixes $(s,\emptyset)$. RIGHT: transition main at $(l,b)$, roles $(\mathsf M,\mathsf T,\mathsf S)$, rates $(f_l,b,\min(a,b))$, suffixes $(\emptyset,t)$. Coefficient $w_bf_l/\pi_{f_l}$; midpoint channel $\mathsf M$ at rate $f_l$.\\
Subtraction & Actual main round $K$ at stage $l$, unchanged roles, rates $(u,f_l,\min(a,f_l))$, suffixes $(s,t)$; coefficient $-w_{f_l}$.\\
Copy & Residual main at stage $l-1$, route $\beta$, unchanged roles, rates $(u,b,\min(a,b))$, suffixes $(\alpha s,\beta t)$; coefficient $w_b$. For $\alpha>0$, detector children $U_{l-1,h}$, $1\le h\le K$, channel $\mathsf S$, intrinsic rate $f_{l-1}$, suffix $\alpha s$. Their maximum goes through $\chi_{1/4,1/2}$; for $\alpha=0$ the multiplier is one.\\
Signal & This main's own preparation with identical kind, stage, round, route, roles, $u,a,s,t$, but usage $a$; coefficient $\zeta$. Outer averaging still uses original usage $\tau$.\\
Detector & For $U_{l,i}[c,s]$, score row at $(l,i)$, roles $(c+1,c,c+2)$ modulo three, rates $(f_l,f_l,f_l)$, suffixes $(\emptyset,s)$; the entire incoming $j_{\rm det}$-rank is one operand.\\
Direct reward & For $W_l[c,u,s]$ at $x_0\alpha$, lower $W_{l-1}[c,u,\alpha s]$ and the same intrinsic copy detectors as above. Coefficient one.\\
Product reward & LEFT: actual main at $(l-1,K)$, roles $(c,c+1,c+2)$, rates $(u,f,f)$, suffixes $(\alpha s,\emptyset)$, $f=f_{l-1}$. RIGHT: $W_{l-1}[c+1,f,\emptyset]$. Coefficient $f/\pi_f$, same copy multiplier and midpoint mask.\\\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
Neither RIGHT tuple contains an old source, old source rate/suffix, left port or
ancestor word. A relative traversal record may retain a left token for returning;
that token is not a semantic field of RIGHT.

definitions.title: Complete normalized arrival expressions
definitions.tex:
Let $\omega=(-1)^\epsilon512^{-\ell_{\rm mix}h}$ and $H_d=2^{\lambda d}$.
A row leaf below is the child's final stream normalized by $H_*$; vector and
rank leaves have scale one. The normalized expressions are:
\begin{center}\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{lX}
\toprule Tag & Expression at scale $H_d$\\\midrule
Base & labelled base weight divided by $aH_d$ (pilot/actual/score stage-zero base uses $a=f_0=1$).\\
Direct & $(\omega w_bH_*/H_d)\,B$.\\
Product & $(\omega w_b(f_l/\pi_{f_l})H_*^2/H_d)\,F B$.\\
Subtraction & $-(\omega w_{f_l}H_*/H_d)\,F_K$.\\
Copy & $(\omega w_bH_*/H_d)\,r_\alpha B^{D,\beta}$.\\
Signal & $(\omega\zeta H_*/H_d)\,P$, coordinate two only.\\
Detector & $(\omega/H_d)\,R$, the whole incoming score rank.\\
Direct reward & $(\omega/H_d)\,r_\alpha W$.\\
Product reward & $(\omega(f/\pi_f)H_*/H_d)\,r_\alpha F_KW$.\\\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}\end{center}
Products are left-associated in this order; each occurrence of a leaf recomputes
the same stream. A wrong coordinate is zero without deleting presence. A present
left port includes its midpoint hit. The signal's original narrow hit is checked
by VALID, so no extra importance coefficient is introduced. The direct and
product reward records sum to the one fixed reward family before the statistical
analysis; their separate records do not authorize independent seeds.

definitions.title: Fixed representation tests
definitions.tex:
At slack $d$, retain a representative iff
$2N_P(M/H_d)-3N_P(u/H_d)>0$, $P=(\lambda+c_1)d+8$.
At final slack, CLASS uses the complete signed prefixes through a fixed $P_*$
with $6H_1 2^{-P_*}\le\delta_0/10000$ and the separated thresholds in its
algorithm. Neither test depends on a later requested value digit. The reference
uses the same canonical expression trees, prefix places and strict tie choices.
Their comparison with earlier source floor-prefix conventions remains an open
representation lemma, not an unnoticed substitution.

definitions.title: Shared and retained storage
definitions.tex: One root environment, master seed, current vertex, input-position counters and regeneration buffer occupy $O(B)$ bits in total. Scratch is erased before a lower call. A caller retains only its relative task/word/code, numerical resume state, reserved argument cells, actual inverse tokens and owned terminal traces. These are separate from shared scratch. Let $q\ge1$ be the metadata factor fixed in \Dref{D-RESOURCE}: every stated retained-length bound includes all delimiters, locators, flags, zero reservations and input-head positions. No full vertex or absolute tuple is saved in each frame. List terms, operand requests, visits and certificate passes are sequential.

definitions.title: The proposed space allowance and call decreases
definitions.tex:
Let $s$ be an operation stratum from a finite table, and let $s_{\rm op}$ bound it.
At slack $d$ and budget $m$ use the candidate allowance
\[
 w=k_1(1+m)-(k_0+s)d,
 \qquad k_0>s_{\rm op}+1,\quad k_1>2(k_0+s_{\rm op}+1).
\]
At the same $(m,d)$ a child must have larger stratum. An old-prefix child uses
$2d$; a sample child decreases $m$ by at least $d$. A final multiplier decreases
$m$ by $c_{\rm col}$ at fixed final slack. These are proposed forms, not a
completed assignment of strata to every mode. A caller must not claim the
old-prefix decrease for a visit to the current raw row.

definitions.title: A common space hypothesis with a metadata factor
definitions.tex:
Fix an integer $q\ge1$, a root allowance $1\le w_0=O(B)$ and root place $0\le t_0\le9$. Each genuine call has positive integer allowance $w$ and place $t\ge0$. For fixed constants $A,D,c$, every child boundary must satisfy
\[
 \Delta w=w-w'\ge1,\quad j-t\le c\Delta w,\quad
 R_e\le q[A\Delta w+D(t-j)].
\]
The bottom active region uses at most $q(Aw+Dt)$ bits; all other simultaneously live storage, including root enumeration and shared scratch, uses $O(B)$ bits. Regions are disjoint, and a fixed probe-copy overhead has already been included in $R_e$. The largest visited tape address is at most a fixed multiple of this live extent. Both directions of cleanup obey the same hypotheses. These are requirements on an explicit finite source library, not admission tests used to reject a genuine computation.

definitions.title: Arguments, results and elementary work
definitions.tex:
An assignment $r\gets\Call{P}(q)$ names a call and binds its result. Tuple
bindings name every returned component that is used; an unused component is
written $\bot$ or a named unused variable. A case-dispatched call names every
possible target in its algorithm. A REQUEST is a returned message, not a call:
the client must explicitly invoke its listed handler and send the answer back.

Logical inputs are finite stored arrays, lists and exact rationals. Their
elementary operations are scalar rational arithmetic, comparisons, assignments,
array indexing and finite loops; matrix multiplication and a variable-length
rank have named algorithms. Fixed-degree scalar polynomials and fixed-length
min/max formulas use those scalar operations. Physical elementary operations are
bounded-symbol edits, reads of already supplied fields, and finite integer
arithmetic in the explicitly charged work area. A field that requires deriving a
child tuple or transforming its seed is obtained from P-CHILD/P-REPLAY. A expression
name is not permission to execute an unspecified program.

definitions.title: Semantic tasks and physical argument views
definitions.tex:
The symbol $\mathcal T$ means the task record of \Dref{D-TASKS}, with immutable root parameters
available. A logical caller may store that entire record. A physical caller
passes a completed relative handle and mode-specific fields; it does not save
an $O(B)$ absolute tuple in every frame. Its semantic fields can be reconstructed
in one shared $O(B)$ buffer by P-REPLAY. Brackets such as $\mathcal T[2d]$ denote a
complete old-prefix request: same owner, budget and seed, slack replaced by
$2d$. They do not execute an evaluator. Child symbols $Q.L,Q.R$ are the LEFT and
RIGHT relative schemas returned by P-CHILD, not copied source vertices.

A numerical port request adds a port, coordinate and place. A terminal request
adds its mode and, for return/discard, the actual trace returned by that same
terminal. A graph handle $G$ owns one continuously allocated raw region and its
cursor; a virtual view borrows a frozen region plus a bounded edit. The exact
bit-level marked-field accessor, complete-link layout and per-phase slot
assignment are not yet supplied: this is U-CATALOG. Field-view notation in the
proposed schedules therefore carries an explicit unresolved implementation
premise; it is not an uncounted completed access algorithm.

definitions.title: Restoration and child boundaries
definitions.tex:
A restoring query returns a bounded answer and restores the cursor and every shared mutable register not explicitly designated as output. A successful paired move returns its actual opposite token:
\[
 \Call{Fwd}_{\mathcal T}(x,p)=(y,r)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Call{Inv}_{\mathcal T}(y,r)=(x,p).
\]
Failure restores the starting cursor. A retained terminal trace owns its child records; its ancestor may perform only preallocated finite completion actions until RETURN or DISCARD consumes it. Complete invalid requests have local restoring failure; incomplete arguments authorize no call.
At a genuine boundary $(w,t)\to(w',j)$, the proposed bound is
\[
 0<w'<w,\quad j-t\le C_e(w-w'),\quad
 R_e\le q\{A_e(w-w')+D_e(t-j)\}.
\]
Here $R_e$ is the entire caller-owned retained region. These inequalities must be proved before guards are installed. \Dref{D-RESOURCE} specifies their simultaneous use; a list of fields alone does not establish them.

definitions.title: Closed numerical syntax and named leaves
definitions.tex:
An expression is a finite tree built from rational/dyadic constants, named
restoring digit leaves, affine sums, products, min/max, interval clipping,
reciprocal after clipping to a fixed positive interval, and finite padded ranks.
Only the following variable lists occur: descriptor sums, representative-pool
ranks, raw-port ranks and the incoming rank provided by P-INCOMINGRANK. They have
explicit finite lengths and defaults; a new arbitrary program cannot be inserted
as a expression. All other expression depth and round maxima are fixed constants.

Each node has a power-of-two scale enclosing its range for independent operands.
Affine bounds use the sum of coefficient magnitudes times operand bounds;
products use their product; min/max use the larger bound; projection first uses
a common scale enclosing its input and both endpoints. A reciprocal has a fixed
positive interval and a captured originating place. Its factor $C$ is undone
only after proving the adapted output normalized. A shift $2^sx$ uses
$N_{t+s}(x)$, or zero for $t+s<0$; its residue uses the last at most $\kappa$
difference digits. This shift is legal only with the output range promise.

A cutoff first clips its argument to $r\in[0,1]$, computes $a=r^2$, $b=ar$,
$c=(10-15r+6a)/32$, then $bc$, and finally projects $32bc$ to $[0,1]$ at a
common scale enclosing the input. Thus no oversized intermediate is passed as a
unit stream. Maxima have increasing-index leaves and left ties. Public rational
leaves use Euclidean signed-floor certificates; their numerator, denominator,
remainder and bit scans are pure shared work, erased before an estimator call.

\begin{longtable}{p{.22\textwidth}p{.70\textwidth}}
\toprule Client & Exact expression and external leaves\\\midrule\endhead
INTRINSIC\allowbreak VALUE & \Dref{D-INTRINSIC} expression; lower ROW, VECTOR, INCOMING leaves and explicitly paired right-factor visits.\\
MERGE & One old coordinate/default plus every matched new arrival, then size $\max(W^1,-W^1,W^2,-W^2)$ when requested. Old adapter and sign are part of the tree.\\
INTER\allowbreak MEDIATE\allowbreak RANK & Pool slots plus $k$ extra old defaults. Each nonrepresentative slot supplies old default, not zero.\\
THRESHOLD & $u=\max(z,2^{-c_1d},\operatorname{rank}_{n_d}M)$ or $q=\max(0,\operatorname{rank}_{k_{\rm row}}W^1)$; rank and old-default leaves.\\
COMPRESS /\allowbreak RAWNUM default & $z'=\max(u,\min(q,3u))$; compression uses the unclamped center and common scale $8H_d$; default is $\min(z',R_d)$.\\
SCALARPREFIX & Old scalar plus every arrival, projected to $[-R_d,R_d]$; top old scalar is zero.\\
RAWRANK & Constant raw-port list with absent-port defaults and $k$ appended defaults.\\
LOCAL & \Dref{D-LOCAL} and witness $I$; raw first/second coordinate, raw rank and narrow-mask leaves.\\
ROW & Local factor times incoming gate and, for mains, $\gamma$ of the fixed detector-round maximum. Every detector is an individual lower VECTOR leaf.\\
VECTOR & Base public reward, or $\operatorname{clip}_{[0,1]}(H_1\cdot\mathrm{SCALARPREFIX})$.\\
INCOMING gate & $1-\chi_{1/4,1/2}(\mathrm{INCOMINGRANK})$.\\\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
The reference computation stores both rational values and these canonical trees.
Its rank trees use the same pool/default list, rather than replacing it by a
numerically equal but certificate-different list. \Aref{L-CERT} evaluates the
finite integer rules directly on those trees. Proving that the physical
